guides.summary: Every interactive component is built on React Aria, which implements the WAI-ARIA patterns and is tested across browsers and screen readers. That covers the mechanics. Whether a screen is accessible still depends on what you put in it.
guides.text:
# Accessibility

Every interactive component is built on [React Aria](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/),
which implements the WAI-ARIA patterns and is tested across browsers and screen
readers. That covers the mechanics. Whether a screen is accessible still depends
on what you put in it.

## What every component gives you

- **Names and descriptions wired up.** A field's label, help and error are linked
  to its input, so they are read together.
- **Keyboard support** for each pattern: arrow keys in menus, lists, tabs and
  grids; Escape to close overlays; Space and Enter where expected.
- **Visible focus** only for keyboard users, with a focus ring that meets contrast.
- **Focus management** in overlays: focus moves into a dialog, stays there, and
  returns to the trigger when it closes.
- **Announcements** for changes people can't see, such as sort order, selection
  and notifications.
- **Reduced motion** respected, and controls at least 24px tall even in the compact register.

**Example:** Tab into these: focus shows, the error is read with its field, and the select opens with the keyboard.

```tsx
<VStack gap="lg">
  <TextField label="Membership number" defaultValue="SQ-104" error="Enter all 6 digits, like SQ-104-772" />
  <Select label="Night-watch frequency" placeholder="Choose one" options={[{ value: "monthly", label: "Monthly" }, { value: "two-monthly", label: "Every two months" }]} />
  <HStack gap="sm" align="center">
    <Button variant="primary">Save</Button>
    <IconButton icon={<PrintIcon />} label="Print this report" />
  </HStack>
</VStack>
```

## What your app still has to do

- **Write real labels.** Every field has a visible label; every icon-only button
  has a `label`. A placeholder is not a label.
- **Structure the page.** One `h1`, headings in order, landmarks from `Page`,
  `Header` and `Sidebar`.
- **Write errors people can act on.** "Enter your email address", not "Invalid".
- **Keep a sensible focus order** when you compose components, and move focus on
  purpose after big changes, such as to the error summary after a failed submit.
- **Check custom colours.** The library tests its own text and surfaces; brand
  overrides, text on images and translucent panels are yours to check (4.5:1 for
  text, 3:1 for large text and control edges).
- **Don't use colour alone** to show status, selection or errors.

**Example:**

```tsx
<Alert tone="warning" title="Colour is never the only signal">
  Badges, alerts and field errors always say the status in words; the colour only supports it.
</Alert>
```

## Testing

Use the keyboard alone through each task, zoom to 200%, try a phone width, and run
a screen reader (VoiceOver or NVDA) over new screens. Automated checks such as axe
catch missing names and contrast, but not whether the experience makes sense. See
[Focus management](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-focus-management) and
[Labels, help and validation](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-labels-help-and-validation).

guides.title: Colour
guides.summary: Colour carries meaning, so it is used sparingly: a calm neutral page, Squonk blue for the thing to act on, and status colours only when something has a status. Every swatch below is read from the theme you are viewing; switch light and dark in the toolbar, or change a colour in the Theme panel, and they follow.
guides.text:
# Colour

Colour carries meaning, so it is used sparingly: a calm neutral page, Squonk
blue for the thing to act on, and status colours only when something has a
status. Every swatch below is read from the theme you are viewing; switch light
and dark in the toolbar, or change a colour in the Theme panel, and they follow.

## Brand and action

| Colour | Token | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accent | `--squonk-roles-color-accent` | The leading action, selected states, progress. |
| Accent, pointed at | `--squonk-roles-color-accent-hover` | The accent under the pointer. |
| On accent | `--squonk-roles-color-on-accent` | Text and icons on the accent. |
| Link | `--squonk-roles-color-link` | Links in running text. |

**Example:**

```tsx
<HStack gap="sm" wrap align="center">
  <Button variant="primary">Pay now</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary">Set up a plan</Button>
  <Text>Read the <Link href="#colour">payment options</Link>.</Text>
</HStack>
```

**The brand colour is a fill.** Use Squonk blue for buttons, selections and
highlights. Links use the link colour, which is tuned to read as body text on
every background.

## Text

| Colour | Token | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text | `--squonk-roles-color-text` | Body text and values people type. |
| Supporting | `--squonk-roles-color-text-supporting` | Descriptions, captions and meta. |
| Hint | `--squonk-roles-color-hint` | Help under a field. |
| Quiet | `--squonk-roles-color-text-quiet` | De-emphasised text. Keep it readable. |
| Error text | `--squonk-roles-color-invalid-text` | Error messages. |

## Surfaces and lines

| Colour | Token | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page | `--squonk-roles-color-page` | Behind content. |
| Surface | `--squonk-roles-color-surface` | Cards, menus, popovers and dialogs. |
| Well | `--squonk-roles-color-well` | Recessed areas: tracks, code, skeletons. |
| Hover | `--squonk-roles-color-hover` | A row or quiet button under the pointer. |
| Selected | `--squonk-roles-color-selected` | A selected row or option. |
| Backdrop | `--squonk-roles-color-backdrop` | The dimmed page behind a dialog. |
| Divider | `--squonk-roles-color-divider` | Lines between rows and sections. |
| Field border | `--squonk-roles-color-field-border` | The edge of a field at rest. |
| Focus ring | `--squonk-roles-color-focus-ring` | The keyboard focus indicator. |

## Status

Status colours always come with words: a colour alone must never be the only way
to tell an error, a warning or success. Use them through the `tone` of a
[Badge](squonk-ui://components/badge) or an
[Alert](squonk-ui://components/alert), and say the status in their text.

**Example:**

```tsx
<VStack gap="md">
  <HStack gap="sm" wrap>
    <Badge tone="neutral">Draft</Badge>
    <Badge tone="info">Processing</Badge>
    <Badge tone="success">Paid</Badge>
    <Badge tone="warning">Due soon</Badge>
    <Badge tone="error">Overdue</Badge>
  </HStack>
  <Alert tone="success" title="Sighting logged">We've received your sighting report for 12 September.</Alert>
  <Alert tone="error" title="Payment failed">Your bank declined the payment. Try another account.</Alert>
</VStack>
```

## Light and dark

Every colour has a light and a dark value; components pick the right one. A
section can take the opposite mode with `ThemeStyleBlock invertMode`, and text on
it stays readable.

**Example:** The same components inside ThemeStyleBlock invertMode.

```tsx
<ThemeStyleBlock invertMode>
  <Block background="default" padding="md" radius="md">
  <VStack gap="sm">
    <Alert tone="info" title="Inverted section">Components recompute their colours for the opposite mode.</Alert>
    <HStack gap="sm" wrap>
      <Button variant="primary">Continue</Button>
      <Badge tone="warning">Due soon</Badge>
    </HStack>
  </VStack>
  </Block>
</ThemeStyleBlock>
```

## Checking your own colours

The library tests contrast for its own text roles on its own surfaces. Custom
colours, brand overrides, translucent panels and text over images are yours to
check: aim for 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text and the edges of
controls. Change colours in the theme, not in component CSS; see
[Theme](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-theme) and
[Purpose tokens](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-purpose-tokens).

guides.title: Icons
guides.summary: The library exports a curated set of icons named for their meaning (`AddIcon`, `CloseIcon`, `WarningIcon`), not their drawing. The house style is Lucide: outlined, with one consistent stroke. Import icons from `@squonkstack/ui`, never from `react-icons` directly, so a drawing can change in one place.
guides.text:
# Icons

The library exports a curated set of icons named for their meaning (`AddIcon`,
`CloseIcon`, `WarningIcon`), not their drawing. The house style is Lucide:
outlined, with one consistent stroke. Import icons from `@squonkstack/ui`, never from
`react-icons` directly, so a drawing can change in one place.

## Size and colour

Icons take the current text colour and default to the size of the text around
them. Inside a control, use `size="control"` so the icon grows with the
[register](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-space-and-layout).

**Example:**

```tsx
<HStack gap="md" wrap align="center">
  <Button variant="primary"><AddIcon size="control" /> New sighting</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary"><SearchIcon size="control" /> Search</Button>
  <IconButton icon={<SettingsIcon />} label="Settings" />
  <Text tone="warning"><WarningIcon /> Due in 3 days</Text>
</HStack>
```

| `size` | Renders at | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inherit` (default) | The surrounding text size | Icons next to words |
| `sm`, `md`, `lg` | Small, body and large text sizes | Standalone icons |
| `control` | The register's control icon size | Icons inside buttons and inputs |

## Labelling icons

- **Next to words:** the icon is decorative; the words carry the meaning, and the
  icon is hidden from screen readers.
- **On its own in a control:** the control needs a name. `IconButton` requires a
  `label`, which is also shown as its tooltip.
- **On its own as information:** give it a text alternative with `label`.
- Don't put essential instructions only in a tooltip, and don't use an emoji as an
  icon: its look and its spoken name vary by platform.

**Example:** An icon-only button names its action.

```tsx
<HStack gap="sm">
  <IconButton icon={<DeleteIcon />} label="Delete draft" />
</HStack>
```

## The set

Search, then click an icon to copy it.

Need one that isn't here? See [Icon](squonk-ui://components/icon)
for how to add one. Upstream licences (Lucide, Simple Icons, react-icons) are in
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

guides.title: Motion
guides.summary: Motion is small and purposeful. It shows where something came from or went, keeps your place when things change, and draws the eye to what just arrived. It is never decoration that makes someone wait.
guides.text:
# Motion

Motion is small and purposeful. It shows where something came from or went,
keeps your place when things change, and draws the eye to what just arrived. It
is never decoration that makes someone wait.

## How the system fits together

Four layers, each owned by one place, so they never fight:

| Layer | What it decides | Where it lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Character** | How motion feels: tempo, curves, how far things travel, bounce, stagger. | The theme: motion primitives, and the `roles.motion.*` purposes below. |
| **Vocabulary** | What kinds of motion exist: pop, slide, collapse, reveal, swap, glide… | The [Motion components](squonk-ui://components/motion). |
| **Choreography** | How several things move together. | `Motion.Stagger`, and the Layout and Presence components. |
| **Level** | How much motion there is: full, reduced or none. | The device's reduced-motion setting, and `SquonkThemeProvider`'s `motion` prop. |

The library's components already use the Motion components, so a theme
changes how every menu, dialog, toast, tab, table and accordion moves, and an
app's motion level applies to all of them.

## Every theme, the same scene

Press **Play** to run the same scene in each example theme: cards arriving in
sequence, a figure counting to its new value and highlighting, a list
reordering, and a popover under **Details**. Only the theme's motion character
differs: Fieldbook is instant and linear, Tidepool springs, Kauri fades slowly, Monolith slides all at once and Aurora glides. Use **Slow motion** to study the
curves, and **Reduced motion** to see what someone who asks for less motion
gets: fades in place, nothing travelling.

## Character: the theme's motion primitives

A theme sets its motion with six primitives. Every motion duration, curve and
distance derives from them, through the purpose tokens below.

| Primitive | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `transitionDurationMs` | `200` | The tempo. Overlays take this long; arrivals and panels 1.5×; counting figures 2.5×. |
| `motionTravelPx` | `16` | How far things move and grow as they arrive. Overlays grow from `1 − travel ÷ 400` of their size, content rises 1.5 × travel. `0` makes every arrival a plain fade. |
| `motionStaggerMs` | `40` | The gap between items arriving in sequence. |
| `motionBounce` | `0` | How much arrivals overshoot and settle, from 0 (none) to 1. Drawn as a CSS `linear()` spring, so it costs no JavaScript. Off by default: use it for a playful brand. |
| `motionEaseEnter`, `motionEaseExit`, `motionEaseStandard` | Decelerate, accelerate, both | The curves things arrive, leave and move within the page on: a keyword, `cubic-bezier()` or `linear()`. |

```tsx
<SquonkThemeProvider
  primitives={{
    transitionDurationMs: 240,
    motionTravelPx: 20,
    motionStaggerMs: 60,
    motionEaseEnter: "cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)",
  }}
>
```

Try them live in the **Motion** section of the theme panel, which also has
slow motion and the motion levels for previewing.

## Timing by purpose

Components time their movement from motion purposes, so menus, dialogs and
panels all move alike. Things arrive a little slower than they leave, so the
eye can follow them in. Re-point any of them with `roleBindings`, like
`{ "roles.motion.revealEasing": "motion.easings.spring" }`.

| Token | Bound to | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-feedback-in` | transitions.instant | Entering hover, press, focus or a selected state: the response appears the moment it's touched. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-feedback` | transitions.quick | Returning to rest after hover, press, focus or selection: a short fade so the change doesn't flicker. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-overlay` | motion.durations.fast | Overlays opening and closing: menus, popovers, dialogs. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-arrive` | motion.durations.normal | Dialogs, drawers and notifications arriving: slower than they leave, so the eye follows them in. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-panel` | motion.durations.normal | Panels expanding: accordions. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-quick` | motion.durations.fast | Small changes within the page: a colour shift, a chevron turning, a panel closing. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-enter` | motion.easings.enter | Easing for things arriving. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-exit` | motion.easings.exit | Easing for things leaving. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-standard` | motion.easings.standard | Easing for things moving within the page. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-spin` | 800ms | One turn of a spinner: quick enough to read as working. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-spin-reduced` | 1800ms | One turn of a spinner with reduced motion: still turning, so work is visibly happening, but calmly. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-loop` | 1.4s | One pass of a loading shimmer or an indeterminate progress bar. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-loop-reduced` | 3s | One pass of an indeterminate progress bar with reduced motion. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-pulse` | 2.4s | One breath of a live status dot: slow, so it never competes with content. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-reveal` | 550ms | Content arriving as it scrolls into view: long enough to notice, over before it's read. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-reveal-easing` | cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) | Easing for content arriving as it scrolls into view: quick to start, settling gently. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-spring` | motion.easings.spring | Easing for things that arrive and settle: popovers, menus, toasts, content appearing. It overshoots a little when the theme has bounce. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-pop-scale` | motion.scales.pop | The size an overlay grows from as it opens, and shrinks to as it closes: 1 for a plain fade. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-nudge` | motion.distances.md | How far content rises as it appears, swaps in or leaves. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-reveal-offset` | motion.distances.lg | How far below its place content starts as it scrolls into view. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-stagger` | motion.stagger | The gap between items arriving one after another, so a group reads as a sequence. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-swap` | motion.durations.normal | Content swapping in: a tab's panel, loaded content replacing its placeholder. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-layout` | motion.durations.normal | Items gliding to their new place when a list is sorted, filtered or changes. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-count` | motion.durations.slow | A figure counting to its new value. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-highlight` | 1600ms | A change drawing the eye: how long its highlight takes to fade. |
| `--squonk-roles-motion-highlight-color` | color-mix(in srgb, var(--squonk-colors-primary) 16%, transparent) | The highlight on something that just changed, fading back to its own background: a faint tint of the brand colour. |

## Level: how much motion

People who ask their device for reduced motion get it everywhere, with nothing
to set up. Nothing travels or grows: overlays, drawers and content fade in
place; list items move at once; decorative loops stop; spinners slow down.
Colour changes, highlights and fades stay, because they don't move anything.

An app can also choose the level itself:

```tsx
// An in-app "Reduce motion" setting
<SquonkThemeProvider motion={settings.reduceMotion ? "reduced" : "system"}>

// Screenshots and tests: every change is immediate, loops hold still
<SquonkThemeProvider motion="none">
```

`system` (the default) follows the device. `reduced` reduces motion whatever
the device says. `none` turns motion off; it's for tests and screenshots, not
people. The level is published as `--squonk-motion-level-*` custom properties, so
it applies before the page hydrates. Set them on an element to scope a level,
or slow motion (`--squonk-motion-level-time: 4`), to part of a page, as the lab
above does.

## Reveal and stagger

`Motion.Reveal` fades and rises content into place as it scrolls into view.
Inside `Motion.Stagger`, each item waits one stagger step more than the one
before, so a group reads as a sequence. Its timing is the `reveal`,
`revealEasing`, `revealOffset` and `stagger` purposes.

**Example:** Reload the page, or scroll this into view, to see it play.

```tsx
<VStack gap="sm">
  <Motion.Stagger>
    <Motion.Reveal><Card variant="outlined"><Text>Annual dues</Text></Card></Motion.Reveal>
    <Motion.Reveal><Card variant="outlined"><Text>Swamp Fund levy</Text></Card></Motion.Reveal>
    <Motion.Reveal><Card variant="outlined"><Text>Night-watch kit hire</Text></Card></Motion.Reveal>
  </Motion.Stagger>
</VStack>
```

## Rules

- **Respect the motion level.** Never force motion past it: take timing from
  the Motion components and they follow it for you.
- **Never hide content behind motion.** Animated content ends visible and
  readable, and stays available if the animation never runs. Figures that count
  are read out once, at their final value.
- **Animate arrivals and changes, not work.** Page sections, cards and
  notifications arrive with motion; a list re-sorting glides; a recalculated
  total highlights. Fields and text someone is reading or typing into don't
  move.
- **Subtle by default.** A few pixels and a few hundred milliseconds. Bounce is
  a brand choice, off unless a theme asks for it, and never on drawers or
  anything people work in.
- **Keep timing in the library.** Use the components' own motion, or wrap your
  own element in a Motion component. A one-off transition in product code
  drifts from the rest; new motion belongs in the library as a Motion component
  or a motion purpose.

guides.title: Overview
guides.summary: SquonkUI is a small set of decisions applied the same way everywhere: one type family, one spacing scale, a handful of named shapes and colours, and components that already behave correctly for keyboards, screen readers and narrow screens. These pages show those decisions with the real components, in the theme you are viewing.
guides.text:
# Foundations

SquonkUI is a small set of decisions applied the same way everywhere: one
type family, one spacing scale, a handful of named shapes and colours, and
components that already behave correctly for keyboards, screen readers and
narrow screens. These pages show those decisions with the real components, in
the theme you are viewing.

**Example:** Built only from library components and theme tokens.

```tsx
<Card variant="outlined">
  <VStack gap="md">
    <Heading level={3} as="h2">Contact details</Heading>
    <TextField label="Email" defaultValue="aroha@example.org" helperText="We send notices here." />
    <HStack gap="sm" wrap>
      <Button variant="primary">Save</Button>
      <Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button>
    </HStack>
  </VStack>
</Card>
```

## Principles

- **Calm and readable.** Clear hierarchy, generous but deliberate space, one leading
  action per task, and emphasis used sparingly.
- **Named decisions, not numbers.** Components read purpose tokens such as "the gap
  between a field's label and its input", so a theme changes what a purpose means
  in one place. See [Purpose tokens](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-purpose-tokens).
- **Accessible by construction.** Behaviour comes from React Aria: labels, focus,
  keyboard and announcements are built in. Your content still has to be clear.
- **Every state counts.** Empty, loading, error, long-text and phone-width states
  get the same care as the populated desktop screen.

## How the pieces fit

| Layer | What it is | Use it to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Layout primitives | `VStack`, `HStack`, `Cluster`, `Grid`, `Split`, `Container`… | Arrange components; the parent owns placement and spacing |
| Named layouts | `Page`, `Section`, `Card`, `Header`, `Sidebar` | Give common screens a consistent shape |
| Components | Buttons, fields, overlays, tables… | Do the work, with behaviour and accessibility built in |
| Presentation | `compact`, `default`, `large`, `hero` registers | Size a region's controls for its job, from dense admin to marketing |
| Theme | `SquonkThemeProvider`, `ThemeModifier`, `ThemeStyleBlock` | Change primitives, purposes, mode or density for an app or a subtree |

## What the library promises, and what your app checks

The library ships tested components: keyboard and focus behaviour, light and dark
contrast for its own text roles, visual baselines and React Aria semantics. Your
app is responsible for its content and composition: meaningful labels and
headings, the contrast of any custom colours or images, sensible focus order
across the screen, and testing with real data at real widths.

## Foundations

| Page | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Colour](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-colour) | The palette, purpose colours and status tones |
| [Typography](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-typography) | The type scale and the type purposes |
| [Space and layout](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-space-and-layout) | Spacing, registers, breakpoints and layout primitives |
| [Shape and elevation](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-shape-and-elevation) | Corner radii, shadows and surface relief by role |
| [Motion](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-motion) | How motion is themed (tempo, travel, curves, bounce, stagger), the Motion components, and the motion level (reduced motion) |
| [Icons](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-icons) | The icon set, sizes and labelling |
| [Accessibility](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-accessibility) | What you get for free and what you still check |
| [Theme](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-theme) | Primitives, getters, density and theme files |
| [Purpose tokens](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-purpose-tokens) | Every purpose and component token |

For whole compositions (forms, navigation, tables, feedback, overlays) see
[Patterns](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-overview). To find the right component
for a job, start with [Choosing components](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-choosing-components);
for the shape of a screen, [Page layouts and app shells](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-page-layouts-and-app-shells).

## Before adding something new

Start from the user's need and compare it with what exists: a composition of
existing components, a scoped theme change or a new purpose token is usually the
right answer. A new public component needs use and avoid criteria, its states,
keyboard and focus behaviour, responsive behaviour, the tokens it binds to, a live
example and tests. When several teams ask for similar changes, prefer one shared
extension over several local ones.

guides.title: Purpose tokens
guides.summary: A purpose token names why a value is there: "the gap between a label and its field", "the fill behind the current page in a nav list". Components read only these names, never a raw size or colour. A theme decides what each name means, so you can change how a whole product looks by changing a few decisions.
guides.text:
# Purpose tokens A purpose token names why a value is there: "the gap between a label and its field", "the fill behind the current page in a nav list". Components read only these names, never a raw size or colour. A theme decides what each name means, so you can change how a whole product looks by changing a few decisions. This page explains the kinds of purpose tokens, how they bind to one another, and how to change a theme with confidence that it stays coherent. ## Three layers, one direction The theme has three layers, and values flow one way through them: | Layer | Says | Examples | Who reads it | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Primitives and raw values** | How much | `spacingPx`, `fontPx`, `colors.primary`; the scales `spacing.md`, `typography.sizes.sm` | Purpose tokens, and layout props such as `gap="md"` | | **Purpose tokens** | What for | `roles.space.fieldGap`, `roles.color.hint`, `roles.indicator.current.bar` | Every component with that purpose | | **Component tokens** | One component's own decision | `components.button.paddingInline`, `components.illustration.tintStrength` | That component only | A purpose can point at a raw value or at another purpose. A component token can point at a purpose. Nothing points back up a layer. Follow any token and you reach a primitive in a few steps: ```text roles.space.fieldGap → roles.space.related → spacing.xs → spacingPx × 0.5 ``` The Theme panel in Storybook shows this chain for every token on the page. ## Why you can experiment without losing control A theme you can't predict is one you stop changing. Purpose tokens keep a theme predictable with a few rules, so you can try ideas freely and keep the ones that work. - **Every value has one owner and one reason.** Each token has a `why` (shown in the tables below). If two uses share a value but not a reason, they get two tokens, so changing one never surprises the other. - **Decisions flow one way.** Primitives feed purposes, and purposes feed components. A change moves down the chain to everything that depends on it and never sideways into unrelated parts. - **Change at the highest level that's true.** If every gap between related things should grow, change the one tier token they share. If only form fields should, change `roles.space.fieldGap`. The table below maps common wishes to the token to change. - **The theme guards what matters.** Text on a fill never drops below AA contrast, whatever the colours or sliders say. guides.title: Shape and elevation
guides.summary: Corners and shadows are named by role, so every control shares one shape and every floating panel one depth. A theme changes a role once, for example `roles.radius.control` to make every control a pill, and it reaches all of them.
guides.text:
# Shape and elevation

Corners and shadows are named by role, so every control shares one shape and
every floating panel one depth. A theme changes a role once, for example
`roles.radius.control` to make every control a pill, and it reaches all of them.

## Corners

**Example:** Each component takes the radius of its role.

```tsx
<VStack gap="md">
  <HStack gap="sm" wrap align="center">
    <Button variant="primary" shape="rounded">Save</Button>
    <Button variant="secondary" shape="rounded">Cancel</Button>
    <Checkbox label="Remember me" defaultChecked />
  </HStack>
  <TextField label="Reference" defaultValue="DUES-0042" />
  <HStack gap="sm" wrap align="center">
    <Tag>Night watches</Tag>
    <Badge tone="success">Paid</Badge>
    <Avatar name="Aroha Ngata" />
  </HStack>
</VStack>
```

Buttons default to the `pill` shape; use `shape="rounded"` to match fields in
dense forms. Keep one button shape within a task.

### Nested corners

When a rounded shape sits inside another, their curves run parallel: the inner
radius is the outer radius less the gap between them. The library does this
for segments in enclosed tabs and small buttons inside a field or tag, so a
round theme gets round buttons and a square theme square ones. It never goes
below the inner shape's own radius. Do the same in your own nested surfaces:

```css
border-radius: max(var(--squonk-roles-radius-item), calc(var(--squonk-roles-radius-surface) - var(--squonk-roles-space-surface-inset)));
```

Menus and listboxes have the pair worked out already. `radius.listItem` is
`radius.list` less the panel's inset and border. A row can't be rounder than
half its height, so `radius.list` is the surface radius limited to half a row
plus that inset and border: however round the theme, the first and last rows
follow the panel's curve instead of being cut by it. Both follow the surface
radius, the list's spacing and its text size when a theme re-points them. Use
the pair for your own panel of rows:

```css
.menu { padding: var(--squonk-roles-space-list-inset); border-radius: var(--squonk-roles-radius-list); }
.row {
  padding: var(--squonk-roles-space-list-item-inset-block) var(--squonk-roles-space-list-item-inset-inline);
  font-size: var(--squonk-roles-type-list-item);
  line-height: var(--squonk-roles-type-tight-line-height);
  border-radius: var(--squonk-roles-radius-list-item);
}
```

## Elevation

Shadows say how far something sits above the page. Most content sits flat on the
page or in an outlined card; shadows are for things that float.

**Example:**

```tsx
<Grid minColumnWidth="12rem" gap="md">
  <Card variant="outlined"><Text>Outlined: the usual way to group content.</Text></Card>
  <Card variant="elevated"><Text>Elevated: content that should stand forward.</Text></Card>
  <Card variant="filled"><Text>Filled: a quiet, recessed group.</Text></Card>
</Grid>
```

Don't stack a border, a shadow and a bright background on every group: pick one
way to separate it.

## Light and relief

A theme can give surfaces a little relief: a subtle gradient across each one and
a highlight and shade along its edges, so controls look raised off the page and
fields sit slightly into it. It is off by default, and most themes should leave
it off or keep it gentle.

Everything follows one light source. `lightAngle` says where the light comes
from, in degrees clockwise from above, and turns every relief gradient, every
edge and every computed shadow above with it, so the whole interface agrees.
Shadows you write yourself in a role binding (such as a hard `3px 3px 0`) are
used as written, so draw them to match your angle.

| Primitive | Range | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reliefDepth` | 0–1 (default 0) | How far a surface's tone shifts across its face, lit side to far side. |
| `reliefSheen` | 0–1 (default 0) | The strength of the highlight and shade strokes along its edges. |
| `reliefProfile` | `soft`, `bevel`, `glass`, `pillow`, `print` | How the light falls: a smooth gradient, crisp edges, a glossy band, a cushion, or hard embossed edges. |
| `reliefBlend` | `normal`, `soft-light`, `overlay` | How the relief combines with the colour beneath. `soft-light` keeps saturated buttons cleaner. |
| `lightAngle` | 0–359 (default 0) | Where the light comes from. Also turns the drop shadows. |

### Postures

Components don't read the relief directly. Each takes the purpose tokens for its
posture, `roles.relief.<posture>.fill` (a `background-image` over its own colour)
and `.edge` (inset shadows), so a theme can change one posture without the others.

| Posture | Components | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `control` | Buttons (not ghost), select triggers, switch thumbs, the selected segment of enclosed tabs | `relief.raised` |
| `surface` | Elevated, outlined and featured cards | `relief.raisedSubtle`, half the strength |
| `chrome` | The header | `relief.raisedSubtle` |
| `well` | Text fields, text areas, searchable selects, currency fields, switch and segmented tracks, filled cards | `relief.recessed` |
| `pressed` | A button while pressed, a select while pressed or open | `relief.recessed` |

Disabled controls and ghost buttons stay flat. Re-point a posture at a
per-profile token to give it a profile of its own: here controls are cushions
and fields have crisp bevels, under one light from the upper left.

Relief is decoration: it never carries meaning, and text must stay readable at
the darkest and lightest points of a gradient. Keep depth low on large surfaces,
check dark mode (highlights are toned down there automatically) and keep the
light above the horizon: light from below reads as wrong.

guides.text:
# Space and layout

Space comes from one scale built on an 8px step (the `spacingPx` primitive).
Components don't pick steps directly; they use space purposes, so every field,
dialog and list spaces itself the same way.

## The scale

| Token | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `--squonk-spacing-none` | 0px |
| `--squonk-spacing-xxs` | 2px |
| `--squonk-spacing-xs` | 4px |
| `--squonk-spacing-sm` | 8px |
| `--squonk-spacing-md` | 16px |
| `--squonk-spacing-lg` | 24px |
| `--squonk-spacing-xl` | 32px |
| `--squonk-spacing-xxl` | 48px |
| `--squonk-spacing-gutter` | 8px |
| `--squonk-spacing-container-padding` | 16px |
| `--squonk-spacing-card-padding` | 16px |

## Space by purpose

**Example:** questionGap between questions, fieldGap inside each one, actionGap between the buttons.

```tsx
<VStack gap="lg">
  <TextField label="Household name" helperText="As it should appear on your membership card." />
  <TextField label="Email" type="email" />
  <HStack gap="sm" wrap>
    <Button variant="primary">Continue</Button>
    <Button variant="ghost">Back</Button>
  </HStack>
</VStack>
```

The full list, with every purpose's reason, is on
[Purpose tokens](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-purpose-tokens).

## Registers

`Presentation` sets the size of a region's controls for its job: `compact` for
dense admin screens, `default` for most of an app, `large` and `hero` for landing
and marketing pages. Control heights, padding and text all step together, so a row
of mixed controls always lines up. When to use each is on
[Density and registers](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-density-and-registers).

## Breakpoints

Layouts are mobile first: they start as one column and add columns as space allows.

| Name | From | Typical change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mobile` | 480px | Larger phones: side-by-side buttons |
| `tablet` | 768px | Sidebars appear; two-column forms |
| `desktop` | 1024px | Full app layouts |
| `wide` | 1280px | Extra columns, wider tables |

Test real narrow containers, not only the window width: a card in a sidebar is
narrow on any screen.

## Arranging components

The parent owns placement and spacing; children size themselves. Reach for a
layout primitive before writing layout CSS.

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Stack things vertically | [VStack](squonk-ui://components/vstack) |
| A row, wrapping if needed | [HStack](squonk-ui://components/hstack) or [Cluster](squonk-ui://components/cluster) |
| Content on one side, actions on the other | [Split](squonk-ui://components/split) |
| A collection of cards | [Grid](squonk-ui://components/grid) |
| Limit reading width | [Container](squonk-ui://components/container) |
| A padded, painted region | [Block](squonk-ui://components/block) |
| A bounded scrolling area | [ScrollBox](squonk-ui://components/scroll-box) |
| Keep media in proportion | [AspectRatio](squonk-ui://components/aspect-ratio) |
| A full screen with header and sidebar | [Page](squonk-ui://components/page) |

Avoid nested scroll areas unless the task needs them; a wide table may scroll
sideways while the page stays put. Use `gap` on the parent rather than margins on
repeated children.

For whole screens (app shells, reading pages, landing pages, resizable
workspaces) and how they change across breakpoints, see
[Page layouts and app shells](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-page-layouts-and-app-shells).

guides.title: Theme
guides.summary: The theme has three layers:
guides.text:
# Theme

The theme has three layers:

1. **Primitives:** a few raw inputs, such as `spacingPx: 8`, `fontPx: 16`,
   `controlRadiusPx`, the light and dark colour palettes, and the light and
   relief settings (`lightAngle`, `reliefDepth`, `reliefSheen`,
   `reliefProfile`, `reliefBlend`).
2. **Raw tokens:** scales derived from the primitives (`spacing.md`,
   `typography.sizes.sm`, `colors.text.secondary`). Each is a getter, so changing a
   primitive changes every token derived from it.
3. **Purpose tokens:** what each value is for (`roles.space.fieldGap`,
   `roles.color.hint`). Components read only these. See
   [Purpose tokens](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-purpose-tokens).

```tsx
<SquonkThemeProvider
  primitives={{ spacingPx: 10, colors: { primary: "#0b7a5c" } }}  // scale everything
  roleBindings={{ "roles.space.questionGap": "spacing.xl" }}        // change one decision
>
```

## Example themes

Pick a theme from the **Theme** menu in the toolbar, the introduction or the
Theme panel to see every story and docs page in it: Squonk (the default),
Kauri, Fieldbook, Tidepool, Meridian, Monolith, Wayfinder and Aurora. Each
changes only the theme (palette in both modes, type, density, shape, borders,
depth, relief, motion, selection and purpose decisions), so you can
see how far the same components go. Try a button and a field in each: they
behave differently too. [Theme showcase]
puts their buttons, fields and figures side by side, with the purpose decisions
each one makes.

| To change | Re-point |
| --- | --- |
| How far a lifted button rises on hover | `roles.interaction.hoverLift` (`0px` keeps it flat) |
| How much a button squeezes when pressed | `roles.interaction.pressScale` (`0.96` for a soft squeeze) |
| A glow beside a focused button's ring | `roles.interaction.focusGlow` (a box-shadow) |
| A shadow under the primary or a secondary button | `components.button.primary.shadow`, `components.button.secondary.shadow` |
| Outlined or filled secondary buttons | `components.button.secondary.background`, `.border`, `.text` |
| A focused field's halo and its strength | `roles.interaction.fieldFocusHalo`, `roles.interaction.fieldFocusStrength` |
| An underline on a focused field | `roles.interaction.fieldFocusUnderline` (`-2px`) |
| Boxed, underlined or borderless fields | `roles.control.fieldBorder` (`0 0 1px` underlines, `0` for none) |
| Filled fields | `roles.color.fieldBackground` (`colors.background.subtle` for a filled well) |
| A shadow under fields | `roles.elevation.field` (an inset recesses them; a hard offset prints them) |
| Button label case and spacing | `roles.type.buttonCase`, `roles.type.buttonTracking` |
| Raised controls and recessed fields | The `reliefDepth` and `reliefSheen` primitives; see Light and relief in [Shape and elevation](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-shape-and-elevation) |
| One posture's relief profile | `roles.relief.control.fill` and `.edge` (or `surface`, `chrome`, `well`, `pressed`) to `relief.glass.raised.fill` and so on |

The Theme panel's edits sit on top of the chosen theme. The same screen in
every theme is at the end of [Purpose tokens](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-purpose-tokens).
They're examples for the docs, not exports: write your app's own theme with
`SquonkThemeProvider`.

## Changing part of a page

`ThemeModifier` changes the theme for a subtree. Here the second row re-points
the control radius purpose, so its controls are square:

**Example:**

```tsx
<VStack gap="md">
  <HStack gap="sm" wrap align="end">
    <TextField label="Reference" defaultValue="DUES-0042" fullWidth={false} />
    <Button variant="primary" shape="rounded">Find</Button>
  </HStack>
  <ThemeModifier override={{ roleBindings: { "roles.radius.control": "borders.radius.none" } }}>
    <HStack gap="sm" wrap align="end">
      <TextField label="Reference" defaultValue="DUES-0042" fullWidth={false} />
      <Button variant="primary" shape="rounded">Find</Button>
    </HStack>
  </ThemeModifier>
</VStack>
```

| Need | Use | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The app's primitives, purposes and mode | `SquonkThemeProvider` | The whole app (or a new scope when nested) |
| A region's control size | `Presentation` (`compact` to `hero`) | Component metrics only |
| A denser or display-scaled region, or the opposite mode | `ThemeStyleBlock` | Rebuilds from the root primitives |
| Specific values for part of a page | `ThemeModifier` | Explicit overrides, kept across later rebuilds |

Some purposes are worked out from others, so they keep up without being
re-pointed themselves. `roles.radius.list` and `roles.radius.listItem`, the
corners of a menu or listbox and of its rows, follow `roles.radius.surface`,
the list's inset and its row size, so rows stay nested in their panel in any
theme. Re-point either one directly to set it yourself.

Keep density separate from global primitives: a compact admin table doesn't
justify shrinking the whole app. `ThemeStyleBlock` is not a uniform zoom: unitless
line heights, icon proportions and some fixed component geometry (avatars,
spinners, switch tracks) stay as they are.

## Colours on painted surfaces

Library surfaces recompute their text colours for their own background, so text
stays readable on cards, wells and inverted sections. Explicit tones, browser-only
colour expressions (`var()`, `currentColor`, `color-mix()`), translucency and
images can't be checked in JavaScript; check those in the rendered page.

## Binding through meaning

Purposes bind through a middle tier of shared decisions, so one change reaches
everything that shares a meaning, while any single purpose can still be
re-pointed on its own:

| Tier | Tokens | What binds to it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Proximity | `roles.space.adjoining`, `related`, `grouped`, `separated`, `distinct` | Every gap, by how related the things it separates are: a label and its field are `related`, buttons in a bar `grouped`, one question and the next `distinct` |
| Text size | `roles.type.fine`, `small`, `body`, `large` | Hints and tooltips (`fine`); labels, meta and list items (`small`); legends and callout titles (`body`); panel titles (`large`); icons match the text they sit beside |
| Edges | `roles.color.edge`, `edgeStrong` | Dividers, outlines, field borders, floating panels, switch tracks, chart gridlines; hovered outlines and axis lines |
| Surfaces | `roles.color.surface`, `page`, `well` | Headers, switch thumbs and chart gaps; secondary buttons and footers; hovers, stripes and disabled fields |

```tsx
// Airier forms: every "related" gap (label to field, icon to text) opens up.
<SquonkThemeProvider roleBindings={{ "roles.space.related": "spacing.sm" }}>
// Only the field gap, nothing else:
<SquonkThemeProvider roleBindings={{ "roles.space.fieldGap": "spacing.sm" }}>
```

## A purpose for each colour mode

A binding is one value for both colour modes, or `{ light, dark }` with one for
each. Each side takes what a single value takes: a token path, another purpose
or a CSS value. Token paths already follow the mode, so use a pair only where
the two modes make different decisions.

```tsx
// Navy headings on the light page, cream ones on the dark page.
<SquonkThemeProvider
  roleBindings={{ "roles.color.heading": { light: "#1d3557", dark: "#f1faee" } }}
>
```

A pair has both modes and nothing else. A theme file with a mode missing or
another field is rejected; in code such a pair is ignored and the default
stays. Inside `ThemeStyleBlock invertMode` the other side applies. Check the
contrast of a colour pair in both modes.

## Page background image

`components.page.backgroundImage` paints an image over the page colour: a
gradient or wash behind the whole page. It is `none` by default. `Page` paints
it, and so does the document body when the provider has `withGlobalStyles`. It
is held to the screen while the page scrolls and doesn't repeat, so a gradient
covers the viewport once.

```tsx
<SquonkThemeProvider
  withGlobalStyles
  roleBindings={{
    "components.page.backgroundImage": {
      light: "linear-gradient(180deg, #ffffff, #eef2ff)",
      dark: "radial-gradient(circle at top, #1e1b4b, #020617)",
    },
  }}
>
```

Text on the page is still picked to read on the page colour, so keep the image
close to that colour, and check the page in both modes.

## Quiet tones

A tone's soft fills (a subtle badge, an alert's wash, the tinted current item)
are a light version of the tone in light mode and a deep version in dark mode.
Set `softToneStrength` between 0 and 1 to make them a quiet tint instead: the
surface colour with that share of the tone mixed in. 0.1 to 0.2 keeps tinted
blocks close to the surface in both modes. The text on them is still computed
to stay readable. 0, the default, keeps the built-in fills.

```tsx
<SquonkThemeProvider primitives={{ softToneStrength: 0.12 }}>
```

## Neutral tint

The greys (page, surfaces, wells, text and borders) can lean towards the primary
colour's hue. Set `neutralTint` between 0 and 1: 0 keeps the neutrals as written,
0.3 to 0.7 gives the whole interface a tinge of the brand. Aurora uses 0.6, so
change its primary to teal and its surround turns teal too.

```tsx
<SquonkThemeProvider primitives={{ neutralTint: 0.5, colors: { primary: "#0e7c86" } }}>
```

Each neutral keeps its lightness, so contrast holds, and the tint is strongest in
the mid-tones, fading out at white and black, as hand-tinted greys do. A primary
that is itself grey leaves the neutrals alone.

## Light text on fills

`lightTextBalance` (0 to 100, default 50) decides when text on a coloured fill
(primary buttons, solid badges, ticked boxes) turns light, and how far the fill
deepens to carry it. Higher turns text light on brighter fills and deepens them
further, for richer fills and crisper white text; lower keeps dark text on more
fills and deepens them only to AA. Every pairing still meets AA, whatever the
setting.

| Balance | Light text from | Fill deepened to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Fills white already reads on at 4.5:1, and dark text otherwise wherever it scores higher | 4.5:1 |
| 50 (default) | 3:1 | 4.6:1 |
| 100 | 1.4:1, so even a bright brand colour carries white text | 7:1 |

`textOnFillStrength` (0 to 100, default 50) sets how far that text stands
apart from its fill: at 100 it is pure white or black; at 0 it is a light or dark
tint of the fill itself, just strong enough to read at AA (4.5:1), for quiet,
tonal buttons and badges. The default reads at 7:1.

```tsx
<SquonkThemeProvider primitives={{ lightTextBalance: 80, textOnFillStrength: 100 }}>
```

## Switches

Some theme decisions are yes or no. Each switch sets one or more purposes, so
components follow it without knowing it exists, and a theme can still re-point
any of those purposes on its own.

| Switch | Off (default) | On |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deriveFromPrimary` | Link, focus ring and accent as written | Computed from the primary, moved only as far as their contrast needs (4.5:1 for links, 3:1 for the focus ring), so changing the primary carries the whole brand |
| `primaryGradient` | The primary button in the solid primary | Filled with a gradient from `primaryGradientStart` to the primary at `primaryGradientAngle` (`roles.fill.accent*`), its label picked to read on both ends |
| `uppercaseControls` | Button labels as written | Capitals with a little open tracking (`roles.type.buttonCase`, `buttonTracking`) |
| `underlineLinks` | Links underlined when pointed at | Underlined at rest too (`roles.type.linkDecoration`); a `Link` with its own `underline` prop keeps it |
| `filledFields` | Fields on the surface colour | Filled with the well colour (`roles.color.fieldBackground`); their borders stay |
| `printBackgrounds` | Printed in ink on white | Printed in the theme's own colours (`roles.print.*`) |
| `printLinkUrls` (on by default) | No addresses on paper | Web and email links print their address after the text (`roles.print.linkUrls`) |
| `brandHeadings` | Headings in the text colour | Headings in the brand's readable tone (`roles.color.heading` → `roles.color.link`) |
| `pillControls` | Controls and tags on the radius primitives | Fully rounded (`roles.radius.control`, `roles.radius.chip`) |
| `underlinedFields` | Boxed fields with a focus halo | A single line under each field on the background behind it, and an accent underline on focus |
| `outlinedSecondary` | A quiet neutral secondary button | Outlined in the accent with brand-coloured text and no fill |
| `liftOnHover` (on by default) | Every button stays flat | Lifted buttons rise under the pointer (`roles.interaction.hoverLift`) |
| `squeezeOnPress` | Buttons keep their size when pressed | Buttons shrink a little while pressed (`roles.interaction.pressScale`) |
| `inkShadows` | Soft shadows | Hard offset shadows in the text colour under buttons and fields, falling away from `lightAngle` |
| `strongFocus` | A focus ring two borders wide | A heavier ring (`roles.border.focusWidth`) |

The switches in the second group set purpose bindings directly, the same ones a
theme could write in `roleBindings`, and point them at other purposes where one
fits: `brandHeadings` follows a theme's links wherever they go. A theme's own
`roleBindings` win over a switch, so take a switch and adjust one purpose it sets.

```tsx
<SquonkThemeProvider primitives={{ uppercaseControls: true, underlineLinks: true }}>
```

The default Squonk theme turns on `pillControls`, `squeezeOnPress` and
`primaryGradient`. Kauri turns on `underlineLinks`, `brandHeadings` and
`outlinedSecondary`; Fieldbook `uppercaseControls`, `filledFields` and
`strongFocus`; Tidepool `pillControls`, `filledFields`, `squeezeOnPress` and
`primaryGradient`; Monolith `uppercaseControls`, `underlinedFields` and
`strongFocus`; Wayfinder `underlineLinks` and `strongFocus`; and Aurora
`primaryGradient`. Kauri, Fieldbook, Monolith and Wayfinder turn off
`liftOnHover`. Meridian derives its link, focus ring and accent from its
primary; the others write their own.

A brand drawn as a gradient takes `primaryGradient`. Give the start colour for
each mode; the primary is the end, and the solid primary stays underneath, so
anything that reads `roles.color.accent` (ticked boxes, the active tab) keeps
the solid colour. The label colour is checked against both ends, but check
your own pair too: two ends far apart in lightness leave no colour that reads
well on both.

```tsx
<SquonkThemeProvider
  primitives={{
    primaryGradient: true,
    primaryGradientAngle: 90,
    colors: { primary: "#6d28d9", primaryGradientStart: "#0f766e" },
    darkColors: { primary: "#a78bfa", primaryGradientStart: "#2dd4bf" },
  }}
>
```

With `deriveFromPrimary` and `neutralTint` together, a theme's whole palette
follows one colour: set the primary and the links, focus ring, accent and greys
come with it. For printing, see [Printing](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-printing).

## Navigation indicators

How navigation marks the current page and the item under the pointer is a
theme decision, so every `NavList` in an app agrees. `indicatorStyle` picks one
of `bar` (the default: a bar along the start edge on a quiet fill), `fill`,
`underline`, `ring` (a ring standing off the fill by a gap), `quiet` or `tint`
(a tint of the primary with text to match, and no mark). Each is
a set of `roles.indicator.*` tokens: for the current item and under the
pointer, a background, text colour and mark colour, and the widths of a bar, an
underline and a ring, with the gap between ring and fill. Components draw the
mark from those parts, so any combination is a few values.

```tsx
// A pill-shaped border with a gap around the current page.
<SquonkThemeProvider
  primitives={{ indicatorStyle: "ring" }}
  roleBindings={{ "roles.indicator.radius": "borders.radius.full", "roles.indicator.current.gap": "3px" }}
>
```

Squonk and Tidepool tint, Kauri underlines, Fieldbook stays quiet, Meridian and Wayfinder draw a bar, Monolith fills and Aurora rings.

## What people select

Everything a person chooses or highlights is themed through purposes, so a
theme decides how a choice looks as well as how it moves:

- `roles.color.selected` and `roles.color.onSelected`: the fill and text of a
  chosen option in a select, and of a selected table row.
- `roles.color.selectedMark`: the tick beside the chosen option.
- `roles.type.selected`: the weight of the chosen option, so the choice reads
  without colour.
- `roles.color.textSelection` and `roles.color.onTextSelection`: the highlight
  behind text selected on the page (`::selection`), written by
  `SquonkThemeProvider` with its global styles.

```tsx
<SquonkThemeProvider
  roleBindings={{
    "roles.color.selected": "colors.primary",
    "roles.color.onSelected": "colors.contrastPrimary",
    "roles.color.textSelection": { light: "#efe0b4", dark: "#4a3f1e" },
  }}
>
```

Fieldbook inverts a chosen row to amber, like a terminal; Monolith fills it
black; Kauri marks it in brass and selects text in a pale brass wash.

## Colours of your own

`addedColorPrimitives` (`addedPrimitives` in a theme file) adds a colour to the
theme under a key you choose, with a light and a dark value:

```tsx
<SquonkThemeProvider
  addedColorPrimitives={{ brandTeal: { light: "#0f766e", dark: "#5eead4" } }}
  roleBindings={{ "roles.color.heading": "colors.added.brandTeal" }}
>
```

Each added colour gets:

- **A CSS variable** with its value for the current mode, the key in kebab
  case: `--squonk-colors-added-brand-teal` (`theme.colors.added.brandTeal` in
  TypeScript). A purpose can point at it, as `colors.added.brandTeal` above.
- **A tone palette** like the built-in tones': `--squonk-colors-tone-brand-teal-solid`,
  `-contrast`, `-subtle`, `-on-subtle`, `-outline-text`, `-wash`, `-on-wash` and
  `-wash-border`, computed for the mode. Components that take a `tone` accept
  the key, so `tone="brandTeal"` works where `tone="success"` does.

A built-in tone's name (`neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `error`,
`info`) always means the built-in tone, so give an added colour another key.

## Theme files

The Theme panel exports and imports a theme as JSON (`version: 1`) with
`primitives`, `bindings` (colour getters re-pointed at palette keys),
`addedPrimitives` (custom colours, each with a light and a dark value) and
`roleBindings` (purpose tokens re-pointed). Imports are validated as a whole
before anything changes:

- Colours must be concrete values that both colour parsers understand (hex, RGB,
  HSL, named colours, `transparent`); `var()`, `currentColor` and `color-mix()` are
  rejected because derived colours are computed in JavaScript.
- Numbers must be finite and non-negative; font size, breakpoints and ratios above
  zero; opacity, relief depth and relief sheen between zero and one; the light
  angle below 360. Font families must be non-empty, and the relief profile and
  blend one of their named values.
- Unknown primitives and purposes are rejected. Role bindings must be a token path
  or a CSS value without `;`, braces, angle brackets or comments, or a
  `{ light, dark }` pair of those with both modes and no other field.

Saved panel state is validated the same way on load; invalid parts fall back to
the defaults, so Reset and import keep working.

## Register scaling

| Surface | Follows |
| --- | --- |
| Card, InteractiveCard, Header and Section padding | `presentation.*`, proportional to `spacingPx` |
| Heading sizes | `presentation.headingSizes`, proportional to `fontPx` |
| Control heights, padding and text | `presentation.controlHeight` and the control purposes |
| Gaps, insets and radii | Space and radius purposes |
| Line heights and letter spacing | Fixed ratios |

## Every theme value

The whole theme, layer by layer: the primitives, the raw scales computed from
them, the colours derived for contrast, and the purpose and component tokens
that components read. Each purpose shows what it's bound to (through any other
purposes) and why it exists. Pick a layer or search by name or reason.

It follows the Theme panel live, including re-pointed purposes; switch the mode
in the toolbar to compare light and dark.

guides.title: Typography
guides.summary: One family, Inter, carries every heading and label. It ships with the package (`@squonkstack/ui/fonts.css`) and falls back to Helvetica Neue and Arial. Sizes come from a 16px base, so changing the `fontPx` primitive rescales the whole system.
guides.text: # Typography One family, Inter, carries every heading and label. It ships with the package (`@squonkstack/ui/fonts.css`) and falls back to Helvetica Neue and Arial. Sizes come from a 16px base, so changing the `fontPx` primitive rescales the whole system. ## Headings Choose the heading level for the document's structure, then the look follows. `Heading` takes a `level`, and `as` when the visual level and the element need to differ. ## Text in components Components size their own text by purpose, so a label is a label everywhere: **Example:** ```tsx The message under it, at the supporting size. Paid Meta text, such as "Updated 2 minutes ago" ``` | Token | Bound to | Why | | --- | --- | --- | | `--squonk-roles-type-body` | typography.sizes.base | Running text and the values people type. | | `--squonk-roles-type-small` | typography.sizes.sm | Smaller text beside the body: labels, meta, list items, short notes in a panel. | | `--squonk-roles-type-fine` | typography.sizes.xs | The finest print: hints, descriptions under options, tooltips. | | `--squonk-roles-type-large` | typography.sizes.lg | Text a step above the body: titles of panels and dialogs. | | `--squonk-roles-type-body-line-height` | typography.lineHeights.base | Line height of running text. | | `--squonk-roles-type-label` | roles.type.small | Field labels, legends and table headers. | | `--squonk-roles-type-button-case` | switches.buttonCase | Letter case of button labels (a text-transform): none, or uppercase for a technical voice. Set by the uppercaseControls switch. | | `--squonk-roles-type-button-tracking` | switches.buttonTracking | Letter spacing of button labels: normal, or a little open (0.04em) for uppercase labels. Set by the uppercaseControls switch. | | `--squonk-roles-type-link-decoration` | switches.linkDecoration | Whether links in text are underlined at rest (underline) or only when pointed at (none). Set by the underlineLinks switch. | | `--squonk-roles-type-hint` | roles.type.fine | Help and error text under a field. | | `--squonk-roles-type-legend` | roles.type.body | A group's legend: the question its options answer. | | `--squonk-roles-type-group-hint` | roles.type.small | Help and error text under a group's legend. | | `--squonk-roles-type-meta` | roles.type.small | Secondary text: table cells, breadcrumbs, captions, menu items. | | `--squonk-roles-type-title` | roles.type.large | The title of a panel or dialog, and of the error summary. | | `--squonk-roles-type-callout-title` | roles.type.body | The title of a message inside the content: alerts, toasts, inline notices. Just above its message, so it doesn't compete with the page's headings. | | `--squonk-roles-type-list-item` | roles.type.small | Menu items and listbox options. | | `--squonk-roles-type-supporting` | roles.type.fine | A description under a list option. | | `--squonk-roles-type-tight-line-height` | typography.lineHeights.tight | Line height of single-line labels and controls. | | `--squonk-roles-type-strong` | typography.weights.bold | Weight of labels, titles and emphasis. | | `--squonk-roles-type-selected` | roles.type.strong | Weight of the chosen option in a list or menu, so the choice reads without colour. | | `--squonk-roles-type-regular` | typography.weights.regular | Weight of running text. | | `--squonk-roles-type-font` | typography.fonts.base | The interface typeface. | | `--squonk-roles-type-code-font` | typography.fonts.code | Code, keys and figures that must align. | | `--squonk-roles-type-heading-font` | typography.fonts.heading | The typeface for page and section headings. | ## Body text Use `Text` for running copy. It sizes itself for the [presentation register](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-space-and-layout), and its `tone` sets emphasis: `primary` for content, `secondary` for supporting copy, `muted` only where the text is genuinely optional. **Example:** ```tsx Your annual dues for the 2026–27 season are due on 28 November. You can pay any time before then. We'll remind you a week before. Press Ctrl K to search, or paste the reference DUES-0042. ``` - **Keep lines readable.** Around 45 to 75 characters a line; wrap long copy in a `Container` rather than letting it span a wide screen. - **Sentence case** for headings, labels and buttons ("Save changes", not "Save Changes"). Reserve capitals for badges set with `caps`. - **Don't fake structure.** A big `Text` is not a heading, and screen-reader users navigate by headings. - **Plan for long content.** Names and translated labels get longer; if you truncate, give people a way to see the whole value. - `Code` is for literal machine text; `Kbd` is for keys the interface really supports.

guides.title: Getting started
guides.summary: Set up an app in one command, then build your first screen. About five minutes.
guides.text:
# Getting started Set up an app in one command, then build your first screen. About five minutes. `@squonkstack/ui` and `@squonkstack/ui-mcp` are published to the public npm registry under the MIT licence, so there's nothing to sign in to. ## 1. Run the setup command In your app's folder: ```sh npx @squonkstack/ui ``` First it asks whether to also set up the MCP server for coding agents (`@squonkstack/ui-mcp`), which looks up components and shows the library's stories with live controls. The answer defaults to yes. Then it asks before each step, and running it again changes nothing: 1. Warns if the app's or your home `.npmrc` still sends `@squonkstack` to another registry, which would stop installs from reaching npm. 2. Installs `@squonkstack/ui`, and with the MCP server `@squonkstack/ui-mcp` as a dev dependency, both at the version you ran, so every developer and agent uses the same version. 3. With the MCP server, connects your coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, VS Code with Copilot, Cursor, and Claude Desktop for stories in the chat) to it. 4. Adds a short `@squonkstack/ui` section to `AGENTS.md` (and `CLAUDE.md` for Claude Code) so your agent reads the library's guidance before writing UI. `--yes` accepts every default, `--no-mcp` skips the MCP server, `--agents claude,codex` picks agents, and `--no-install` skips installing. It never edits your code: the next two steps are yours, and it shows the code for them. The setup itself is `npx @squonkstack/ui-mcp init`, which `npx @squonkstack/ui` runs at the same version; it still works on its own. New to using an agent with the library? Read [Working with your agent](squonk-ui://guides/get-started-working-with-your-agent). ## 2. Add the styles and the provider At your app's root, load the font and the component styles once and wrap the app in `SquonkThemeProvider`: ```tsx import "@squonkstack/ui/fonts.css"; import "@squonkstack/ui/styles.css"; import { SquonkThemeProvider } from "@squonkstack/ui/theme-provider"; export function Root({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return ( {children} ); } ``` - `fonts.css` self-hosts Inter; no font CDN needed. - `styles.css` holds every component's styles and the theme's `--squonk-*` variables. Without it, components render unstyled. - `withGlobalStyles` sets the page's background, text colour and font. Leave it off if your app owns its document styles. - `mode="dark"` makes the whole app dark. To change the look, see [Theme](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-theme). The styles are static CSS, so server rendering needs no extra setup. ## 3. Add the lint rules They warn when code rebuilds a control the library has, imports from its internals or hard-codes a colour. They catch the mistakes agents make most: ```js // eslint.config.js import squonkUi from "@squonkstack/ui/eslint"; export default [...squonkUi.configs.recommended /*, your config */]; ``` ## 4. Build your first screen Import each component from its own entry point: ```tsx import { Button } from "@squonkstack/ui/button"; import { Card } from "@squonkstack/ui/card"; import { Heading } from "@squonkstack/ui/heading"; import { Text } from "@squonkstack/ui/text"; import { TextField } from "@squonkstack/ui/text-field"; import { VStack } from "@squonkstack/ui/vstack"; export function CreateWorkspace() { return ( Your workspace Give it a name your team will recognise.
); } ``` Here it is, live: Or ask your agent: *"Build a sign-in form with @squonkstack/ui."* It will look up the components, write the screen and check it in your running app. Ask it to show you a component's stories, and you can try them in the chat. ## Without the setup command Install the packages yourself, then do steps 2 to 4: ```sh npm install @squonkstack/ui "react@^19.2.0" "react-dom@^19.2.0" npm install --save-dev @squonkstack/ui-mcp ``` React and React DOM 19.2 or later are required, on Node 22.14+ or 24.10+. ## Where next - [Foundations](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-overview): colour, type, space and the theme. - [Forms](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-forms-overview): every form works the same way; start here before building one. - [Components]: everything in the library, grouped by what it's for. - [Examples]: complete screens built only from the library. - [Developing the library]: for contributors.

guides.title: Working with your agent
guides.summary: Coding agents build better UI when they know the library as well as you do. SquonkUI gives them four things, all matched to the version your app has installed:
guides.text:
# Working with your agent Coding agents build better UI when they know the library as well as you do. SquonkUI gives them four things, all matched to the version your app has installed: | | What it is | What it does for your agent | | --- | --- | --- | | **MCP server** | `@squonkstack/ui-mcp`, registered as `squonk-ui` | Looks up components and guidance, and shows you the library's stories with live controls | | **Skill** | `use-squonk-ui`, shipped inside `@squonkstack/ui` | Teaches it how the library is meant to be used: setup, composition, forms, theming, accessibility | | **Catalog** | `@squonkstack/ui/catalog.json` | Every component with its imports, props, guidance, patterns and tests | | **Lint rules** | `@squonkstack/ui/eslint` | Flags code that rebuilds a control, reaches into internals or hard-codes a colour | ## Set it up One command, in your app's folder: ```sh npx @squonkstack/ui ``` It asks whether to set up the MCP server (say yes, the default), installs the packages and connects the agents you choose. See [Getting started](squonk-ui://guides/get-started-getting-started) for the registry setup it needs first. | Agent | Where the server is registered | | --- | --- | | Claude Code, including the Claude desktop app's Code tab | `.mcp.json` | | Codex | `.codex/config.toml` (Codex reads it in trusted projects) | | VS Code with Copilot | `.vscode/mcp.json` | | Cursor | `.cursor/mcp.json` | | Claude Desktop chat | Its own user settings, `claude_desktop_config.json` (see below) | Commit the project files, and everyone on the team gets the same setup. It also adds this section to `AGENTS.md`, which most agents read on every task (Claude Code reads it through an `@AGENTS.md` line in `CLAUDE.md`): ```md ## UI: @squonkstack/ui This app builds its UI with `@squonkstack/ui`, Squonk's React component library. - Before writing UI, read the skill that ships with the installed version: `node_modules/@squonkstack/ui/skills/use-squonk-ui/SKILL.md`. - Use the `squonk-ui` MCP server: `find_guidance` and `get_guide` for the design rules, `find_components` and `get_component` before writing UI, and `list_stories` and `preview_story` to show the user a library component or example with live controls. - After UI changes, look at the result in the running app with your browser tools (or ask the user to open the dev server), in light and dark and at a phone width. - Compose library components. Don't restyle them, rebuild what exists, or import from `@squonkstack/ui/dist`. - Run the linter after UI changes; `@squonkstack/ui/eslint` flags native controls and colour literals. ``` Restart your agent afterwards so it loads the server. If you skip the MCP server (`npx @squonkstack/ui --no-mcp`), the second point tells agents to look components up in `@squonkstack/ui/catalog.json` instead, and no agents are connected. Run `npx @squonkstack/ui` again later to add the server. ## The tools | Tool | Arguments | Returns | | --- | --- | --- | | `find_components` | `query` (optional): words for the need, such as `"date input"` or `"empty list"`. Leave it out to list everything. | Matching components from the installed catalog, each with its import path, exports, purpose and the patterns it belongs to | | `get_component` | `id`: a component id (`text-field`), title (`Text Field`) or export name (`TextField`) | One component in full: types, documented sections, accessibility guidance and pitfalls, and links to the guides for its patterns | | `find_guidance` | `query` (optional): what you're designing or deciding, such as `"badge or tag"` or `"confirm delete"`. Leave it out to list every guide. | The design guides that match, each with its summary and sections | | `get_guide` | `id`: a guide id (`patterns-labels-badge-or-tag`) or title (`Labels: Badge or Tag`) | One guide in full: the rules, do and don't examples with their code, and links to the components involved | | `list_stories` | `query` (optional): words for what to show, such as `"searchable select"` or `"dashboard"`
`component` (optional): only this component's stories, by id, title or export name
`limit` (optional): at most this many matches; all by default | Every story shipped with your installed `@squonkstack/ui`, briefly: each component's variants and the example screens, with the id `preview_story` takes. A `query` ranks them, best match first | | `get_theme` | `id` (optional): an example theme to copy, such as `"tidepool"`; absent returns a starter | A theme document to design from: the example theme's, or the library's defaults with what each switch, choice, slider and shared purpose does | | `preview_story` | `storyId`: a story id from `list_stories`, such as `functional-button--primary`
`theme` (optional): `"light"` or `"dark"`; defaults to the host's
`width` (optional): frame width in pixels, 240–2560, such as `375` for a phone
`args` (optional): prop values to start from, such as `{ "variant": "danger" }`
`exampleTheme` (optional): one of the example themes, such as `"tidepool"`
`customTheme` (optional): a theme document you're designing, optionally `basedOn` an example theme
`screenshot` (optional): `true` to also return a PNG and whether it rendered without errors | Shows you the story with a Controls panel for its props, so you can try it | The catalog and guides are also readable as resources, for apps that let you attach context: `squonk-ui://catalog`, `squonk-ui://components/{id}` (such as `squonk-ui://components/button`), `squonk-ui://guides` and `squonk-ui://guides/{id}` (such as `squonk-ui://guides/patterns-labels-badge-or-tag`). ## Checking what your agent built The server doesn't render your agent's code. After it writes UI, ask it to look at the screen in your running app with the browser access it has: a Playwright or browser MCP server, its built-in browser, or you opening the dev server's URL and telling it what you see. That shows the real screen, with your data, routing and providers. ## Stories with live controls `preview_story` shows one of the library's own Storybook stories, the same ones in this site, rendered with the version your app ships. Your agent finds one with `list_stories`, by component or by what you describe. - A **Controls panel** under the story has a control for each prop: switches, text and number inputs, selects and radios, and a JSON editor for lists and objects. Change one and the story updates at once. - A **Theme** editor under the controls shows the theme as a document you can edit, apply and copy into your app. Ask your agent for a look ("warmer, more rounded, a serif heading") and it designs a custom theme the same way. - **Theme** shows it in any of the example themes, **Dark** switches the colour mode, **Width** shows it at phone, tablet or desktop width, and **Reset** puts the story's own values back. Where it shows: - **In Claude Desktop, VS Code with Copilot and ChatGPT** the story appears in the conversation. It's the real component tree, so keyboard, focus, menus and validation all work. - **In Claude Code, Codex and other terminals** the agent gives you a local link (`http://127.0.0.1:/story/`) to the same page. The server's root address lists every story. - **claude.ai in a browser** can't show it: it only connects to servers on the internet, and this one runs on your computer, reading your app's installed packages. Use Claude Desktop for stories in the chat. - **With `screenshot: true`** the agent also gets a picture of the story and whether it rendered without errors. This needs Playwright in your app: ```sh npm install --save-dev playwright npx playwright install chromium ``` The first story takes a few seconds to build and is cached in `node_modules/.cache/squonk-ui-mcp`, rebuilt only when the library changes. ## Stories inline in Claude Desktop Claude Desktop's chat shows stories in the conversation, but it reads its own settings rather than your project's, starts servers outside your app, and doesn't see your terminal's environment. Pick **Claude Desktop** when the setup asks, or add it later: ```sh npx @squonkstack/ui --agents claude-desktop ``` The setup finds Claude Desktop's settings, including the Microsoft Store build's, and points the `squonk-ui` server at your app's installed copy with absolute paths, so it needs no registry token to start. On Windows with WSL it starts the server inside your Linux distro. Claude Desktop runs one `squonk-ui` server at a time: running the setup in another app asks before switching it. Then quit Claude Desktop fully (from the tray or menu bar, not just the window) and reopen it. In a chat, ask *"Show me the @squonkstack/ui Select with its controls"*. To set it up by hand, add this to `claude_desktop_config.json`, with your app's folder and the full path to Node: ```json { "mcpServers": { "squonk-ui": { "command": "/full/path/to/node", "args": ["/path/to/your/app/node_modules/@squonkstack/ui-mcp/dist/cli.js", "--root", "/path/to/your/app"] } } } ``` ## Prompts that work well - *"Show me the @squonkstack/ui Button and let me try its variants."* A good first test. - *"Build the settings page from this sketch. Use the library's form pattern, then check it in the browser on a phone width."* - *"Which component should I use for a list of applied filters? Check the catalog."* - *"Review this screen against the @squonkstack/ui skill and fix anything it rebuilds by hand."* - *"Show me the member dashboard example in dark mode."* Ask for a story when you're choosing between components or variants: you can try each one before your agent writes any code. ## Keep it current The skill, the catalog and the stories always describe the installed version, so updating is just updating the packages, together: ```sh npm install @squonkstack/ui@latest npm install --save-dev @squonkstack/ui-mcp@latest ``` They are released together, with the same version number. Running `npx @squonkstack/ui` again is safe: it only adds what is missing. ## Troubleshooting - **`npx` or `npm` fails with 401, 403 or 404.** The packages are public on registry.npmjs.org and need no sign-in, so an error like this almost always means an old `@squonkstack:registry` line in the app's `.npmrc` or your home `~/.npmrc` is sending npm somewhere else. Remove that line (and any `_authToken` line for the same registry) and try again. - **The agent doesn't see the tools.** Restart it after the setup. Codex reads `.codex/config.toml` only in projects you've marked as trusted. - **The server shows "Connection closed".** Its command couldn't run on the machine the agent runs on. Run `npx @squonkstack/ui-mcp check` in the app's folder: it starts each configured server the way the agent does and says why one fails. - **Claude Code on Windows, app in WSL.** The desktop app's Code tab opening a `\\wsl.localhost\…` folder runs `.mcp.json`'s `npx` on Windows, which usually has no Node. Run `npx @squonkstack/ui-mcp init --windows-client` inside WSL. It adds a launcher that starts the server inside WSL to that folder's local scope in your Windows `.claude.json`, and leaves `.mcp.json` alone. Then restart the session. - **The story link needs a fixed port.** Set `SQUONK_UI_PREVIEW_PORT`. - **Screenshots fail.** Install Playwright and Chromium in the app (see Stories with live controls). ## Working on the library itself This repository has its own `AGENTS.md` and a set of skills for building components, in `.claude/skills/`. See [Developing the library].
