guides.title: Choosing a selection control
guides.summary: `RadioGroup` keeps every option visible, so people can compare them without opening anything. It suits short, meaningful choices (a plan, a delivery speed), especially when each option needs `helperText`. Arrow keys move and select; Tab enters and leaves the group once.
guides.text:
# Choosing a selection control

| Situation | Use |
| --- | --- |
| One choice from a few options that people should compare at a glance | [RadioGroup](squonk-ui://components/radio) |
| One choice from a longer list, or where space is tight | [Select](squonk-ui://components/select) |
| Any number of independent choices | [CheckboxGroup](squonk-ui://components/checkbox-group) |
| One yes/no setting | [Checkbox](squonk-ui://components/checkbox) in a form, or [Switch](squonk-ui://components/switch) for a setting that applies at once (see [Switches, checkboxes and saving](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-switches-checkboxes-and-saving)) |
| Choosing from hundreds of values, or values found by searching | A [Select](squonk-ui://components/select) with `searchable` |

**Example:** Radios for a few options worth comparing, checkboxes for any number, a Select for a long list, and a searchable Select when people know what they're looking for.

```tsx
export function SelectionControlsExample() {
  const [frequency, setFrequency] = React.useState("two-monthly");
  return (
    <Grid columns={{ mobile: 1, tablet: 2 }} gap="lg">
      <RadioGroup
        name="frequency"
        legend="How often do you go on night watch?"
        value={frequency}
        onChange={setFrequency}
        options={[
          { value: "monthly", label: "Monthly" },
          { value: "two-monthly", label: "Every two months", helperText: "Most members" },
          { value: "six-monthly", label: "Every six months" },
        ]}
      />
      <CheckboxGroup
        legend="Which interests do you have?"
        defaultValue={["night-watches"]}
        options={[
          { value: "night-watches", label: "Night watches" },
          { value: "tear-pool-mapping", label: "Tear-pool mapping" },
          { value: "folklore-archive", label: "Folklore archive" },
        ]}
      />
      <Select label="Chapter" placeholder="Choose a chapter" options={CHAPTERS} />
      <Select searchable label="Interest" placeholder="Search by activity" options={[
        { value: "INT-01", label: "Night watches", description: "INT-01" },
        { value: "INT-02", label: "Tear-pool mapping", description: "INT-02" },
        { value: "INT-04", label: "Folklore archive", description: "INT-04" },
        { value: "INT-05", label: "Field photography", description: "INT-05" },
      ]} />
    </Grid>
  );
}

/** Two options hidden behind a select. */
```

## Radio buttons show the options

`RadioGroup` keeps every option visible, so people can compare them without
opening anything. It suits short, meaningful choices (a plan, a delivery speed),
especially when each option needs `helperText`. Arrow keys move and select;
Tab enters and leaves the group once.

**Our rule of thumb:** up to about five options, and when the options are worth
reading side by side, use radios. The sources we checked give no number; this is
our own judgement.

**Do:** Two answers, both visible: one click to answer.

```tsx
export function VisibleFewOptionsExample() {
  return <RadioGroup name="under-18" legend="Are you under 18?" direction="row" options={[{ value: "yes", label: "Yes" }, { value: "no", label: "No" }]} />;
}

// ---- Switches, checkboxes and saving ------------------------------------------

/** A switch that saves at once, says so, and moves back if saving fails. */
```

**Don't:** Two answers hidden behind a select: an extra click, and nothing to compare.

```tsx
export function HiddenFewOptionsExample() {
  return <Select label="Are you under 18?" placeholder="Choose" options={[{ value: "yes", label: "Yes" }, { value: "no", label: "No" }]} />;
}

/** The same two options, visible. */
```

## Select saves space

`Select` hides the options until opened, which saves space but costs a click and
hides the alternatives. Typing jumps to matching options, which matters more as
lists grow (the WAI-ARIA guidance recommends typeahead from about eight options).
Keep option labels short and distinct at the start, so typeahead and scanning work.

`Select` holds one value. For several values, use checkboxes; a select that
silently becomes multi-select confuses keyboard and screen-reader users.

## Checkbox groups

`CheckboxGroup` puts related checkboxes in a `fieldset` whose `legend` states the
question; keep each checkbox's own label short. A parent "select all" checkbox can use
`indeterminate` when only some children are checked.

## Long or open-ended lists

When users know what they are looking for in a long list (countries, people),
they need to type to filter. Add `searchable` to the `Select`: typing filters by
label and description, and `onSearchChange` with `filter={false}` searches a
server instead.

## Settings and disabled options

Whether a choice applies at once or waits for Save is your app's decision; make
it clear and keep it consistent (see
[Switches, checkboxes and saving](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-switches-checkboxes-and-saving)).
A disabled option needs a visible reason when people would otherwise wonder why
they can't pick it. Check keyboard use, long labels and the compact register.

## Related

- [Labels, help and validation](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-labels-help-and-validation)
- [Labels: Badge or Tag](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-labels-badge-or-tag)

---

Sources, paraphrased: [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: listbox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/listbox/),
[combobox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/),
[radio group](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/) and
[checkbox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/checkbox/), © W3C, under the
[W3C Software and Document License](https://www.w3.org/copyright/software-license/);
[React Aria ComboBox](https://react-aria.adobe.com/ComboBox) and
[Building a ComboBox](https://react-aria.adobe.com/blog/building-a-combobox), © Adobe;
[Chakra UI v3 Checkbox](https://chakra-ui.com/docs/components/checkbox) (MIT).

guides.title: Choosing components
guides.summary: Which component should you use? Start from the job the screen has to do, not from the component that looks closest. Find the job below, pick the row that matches, then read the pattern page it links to for the details. If nothing fits, compose existing components before asking for a new one.
guides.text:
# Choosing components

Which component should you use? Start from the job the screen has to do, not
from the component that looks closest. Find the job below, pick the row that
matches, then read the pattern page it links to for the details. If nothing
fits, compose existing components before asking for a new one.

| The job | Start here |
| --- | --- |
| [Do something](#do-something) | Button, IconButton, Link, DropdownMenu |
| [Ask for input](#ask-for-input) | TextField, Select, RadioGroup, CheckboxGroup, Switch, Form |
| [Show a status or a label](#show-a-status-or-a-label) | Badge, Tag, Alert, Meter, Avatar |
| [Give feedback](#give-feedback) | Toast, Alert, field errors, ConfirmModal |
| [Wait for something](#wait-for-something) | Skeleton, Spinner, ProgressBar, Button `pending` |
| [Nothing to show, or it failed](#nothing-to-show-or-it-failed) | EmptyState, Alert |
| [Show more without leaving](#show-more-without-leaving-the-page) | Accordion, Tabs, Popover, Tooltip, Drawer, Modal |
| [Navigate](#navigate) | NavList, Breadcrumb, Tabs, Link, Pagination |
| [Show a collection](#show-a-collection) | Table, a list, Card grid, InfiniteList |
| [Show figures and trends](#show-figures-and-trends) | Stat, Sparkline, charts, Meter |
| [Lay out a page](#lay-out-a-page) | Page, Header, Sidebar, Section, Container, Grid, Split, ResizablePanels |
| [Set the size and voice of a region](#set-the-size-and-voice-of-a-region) | Presentation, Section `register`, ThemeStyleBlock |
| [Words, pictures and icons](#words-pictures-and-icons) | Heading, Text, Icon, Illustration |

## Do something

| You need | Use | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The main action of a form or page | [Button](squonk-ui://components/button) `variant="primary"`, one per area | Several primary buttons competing |
| Other actions beside it | Button `secondary` or `ghost` | A link styled as a button |
| An action shown only as an icon (toolbars, table rows) | [IconButton](squonk-ui://components/icon-button); its label shows as a tooltip | A bare icon with an `onClick` |
| Going to another page | [Link](squonk-ui://components/link), or Button `as="a"` when it must look like an action | A button that changes the URL in code |
| Several actions on one item | [DropdownMenu](squonk-ui://components/dropdown-menu) behind an IconButton | A menu for navigation, or for choosing a value |
| An action that destroys or can't be undone | Button `danger` and a [ConfirmModal](squonk-ui://components/modal) | Confirming everything; offer undo where you can |

Details: [Menus and commands](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-menus-and-commands),
[Destructive actions](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-destructive-actions).

## Ask for input

| You need | Use | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Short text: a name, an email, a search | [TextField](squonk-ui://components/text-field) | A placeholder as the label |
| Long text | [Textarea](squonk-ui://components/textarea) | A TextField that scrolls sideways |
| Money | [CurrencyField](squonk-ui://components/currency-field) | A TextField and your own formatting |
| One choice from a few, worth comparing | [RadioGroup](squonk-ui://components/radio) | A Select that hides two options |
| One choice from many, or where space is tight | [Select](squonk-ui://components/select); `searchable` for long lists | A RadioGroup of twenty |
| Several choices | [CheckboxGroup](squonk-ui://components/checkbox-group) | A multi-select that hides what's chosen |
| One yes or no, submitted with a form | [Checkbox](squonk-ui://components/checkbox) | A Switch inside a form |
| A setting that applies at once | [Switch](squonk-ui://components/switch) | A Checkbox that saves on click |
| Related fields under one question | [Fieldset](squonk-ui://components/fieldset) | A heading that isn't tied to the fields |
| Values, validation and submitting | [Form](squonk-ui://components/form) (`useAppForm`) | Hand-rolled state for each field |

Details: [Choosing a selection control](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-choosing-a-selection-control),
[Forms](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-forms-overview),
[Labels, help and validation](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-labels-help-and-validation),
[Switches, checkboxes and saving](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-switches-checkboxes-and-saving).

## Show a status or a label

| The status belongs to… | Use |
| --- | --- |
| One item: a row, a card, a return ("Overdue", "3 new") | [Badge](squonk-ui://components/badge), with the words in it |
| A category or keyword people may remove or filter by | [Tag](squonk-ui://components/tag) |
| A person or organisation | [Avatar](squonk-ui://components/avatar) with the name beside it, in a [MediaObject](squonk-ui://components/media-object) |
| The whole page or form ("Your annual dues are due in 3 days") | An inline [Alert](squonk-ui://components/alert) |
| A level against a known limit (storage, a credit limit) | [Meter](squonk-ui://components/meter) |
| Work in progress you can measure | [ProgressBar](squonk-ui://components/progress-bar) |

**Example:** The page's status is an Alert, an item's status is a Badge, and a level against a limit is a Meter.

```tsx
export function StatusKindsExample() {
  return (
    <VStack gap="md">
      <Alert tone="warning" title="Your annual dues are due in 3 days">Pay by 28 November to avoid a late fee.</Alert>
      <Cluster gap="sm" align="center">
        <Text weight="bold">Annual dues, 2026–27 season</Text>
        <Badge tone="warning">Due soon</Badge>
      </Cluster>
      <Meter label="Document storage" value={82} warningAt={80} criticalAt={95} valueLabel="8.2 of 10 GB used" showValue />
    </VStack>
  );
}

// ---- Page layouts and app shells ----------------------------------------------

/** A signed-in shell: Sidebar with NavList, then a page header (breadcrumb, title, actions) over the content. */
```

Never use colour alone: every status says its meaning in words. Details:
[Labels: Badge or Tag](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-labels-badge-or-tag).

## Give feedback

| The message… | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Confirms what someone just did and needs nothing more ("Invite sent") | A toast, from [`useToast`](squonk-ui://components/toast) |
| Describes this page or form, and stays until it changes | An inline [Alert](squonk-ui://components/alert) |
| Says what's wrong with one field | The field's `error` |
| Lists everything wrong after a failed submit | The form's error summary |
| Needs an answer before anyone can go on | [ConfirmModal](squonk-ui://components/modal) |

Details: [Toasts, alerts and dialogs](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-toasts-alerts-and-dialogs).

## Wait for something

| You know… | Use |
| --- | --- |
| The shape of what's coming | [Skeleton](squonk-ui://components/skeleton) in that shape |
| Nothing, and it should be short | [Spinner](squonk-ui://components/spinner) that names the work |
| How far along it is | [ProgressBar](squonk-ui://components/progress-bar) |
| It started from a button | Button `pending` |

Details: [Loading and progress](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-loading-and-progress).

## Nothing to show, or it failed

Use [EmptyState](squonk-ui://components/empty-state) for first use, no matches
and no access, each with its own words and next step. A failed load is never
"nothing here": say it failed and offer to try again. Details:
[Empty and error states](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-empty-and-error-states),
[Onboarding and first run](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-onboarding-and-first-run).

## Show more without leaving the page

Pick the lightest surface that works. Each step down this table interrupts more.

| You need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| A section people can open in place (FAQ, advanced options) | [Accordion](squonk-ui://components/accordion) |
| Different views of one thing on the same page | [Tabs](squonk-ui://components/tabs) |
| A name for an icon, or a few words about a term | [Tooltip](squonk-ui://components/tooltip), never anything people need |
| A little content or a few fields beside a control, page still usable | [Popover](squonk-ui://components/popover) |
| A longer side task while the page stays in view (details, filters, an edit) | [Drawer](squonk-ui://components/drawer) |
| A short task or decision that must finish first | [Modal](squonk-ui://components/modal) |
| A long or multi-step task | A page of its own, not an overlay |

**Modal or drawer?** Both block the page. Use a Modal for a short, focused
question or task that needs an answer ("Change bank account", "Delete this
draft?"). Use a Drawer when the task is longer or people need to see the page
behind it for context (a case's details, a filter panel, an edit to one row).
Use neither when the task is long enough to need its own URL.

Details: [Overlays and disclosures](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-overlays-and-disclosures),
[Focus management](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-focus-management).

## Navigate

| You need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Moving between the main pages of an app or section | [NavList](squonk-ui://components/nav-list) in a [Sidebar](squonk-ui://components/sidebar), or horizontal under a [Header](squonk-ui://components/header) |
| Showing where a page sits in a hierarchy | [Breadcrumb](squonk-ui://components/breadcrumb) |
| Switching views of one thing, same URL | [Tabs](squonk-ui://components/tabs) |
| A link in a sentence, or to another site | [Link](squonk-ui://components/link) |
| Moving through pages of records | [Pagination](squonk-ui://components/pagination), or Table `pageSize` |
| The app's menu on a phone | NavList in a [Drawer](squonk-ui://components/drawer) `placement="start"` |

Details: [App navigation](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-app-navigation).

## Show a collection

| People will… | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Compare values across items, sort, select rows | [Table](squonk-ui://components/table) |
| Read items one after another (messages, activity) | A list: `VStack as="ul"` of [MediaObject](squonk-ui://components/media-object) rows |
| Choose between a few items, each a place to go | A [Grid](squonk-ui://components/grid) of [InteractiveCard](squonk-ui://components/interactive-card)s |
| Skim a long feed once, newest first | [InfiniteList](squonk-ui://components/infinite-list) |
| Find items by name or narrow them down | Add search and filters above any of these |

Details: [Lists, tables and cards](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-lists-tables-and-cards),
[Tables and grids](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-tables-and-grids),
[Search, filtering and sorting](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-search-filtering-and-sorting).

## Show figures and trends

| The question | Use |
| --- | --- |
| How much, right now? | [Stat](squonk-ui://components/stat) |
| Which way is it heading? | [Sparkline](squonk-ui://components/sparkline), or Stat `trend` |
| How did it change over time? | [LineChart](squonk-ui://components/line-chart) or [AreaChart](squonk-ui://components/area-chart) |
| How do categories compare? | [BarChart](squonk-ui://components/bar-chart) |
| What is the whole made of? | [DonutChart](squonk-ui://components/donut-chart) for two to five parts |
| Do two measures move together? | [ScatterChart](squonk-ui://components/scatter-chart) |
| What exactly is the value? | [Table](squonk-ui://components/table) |

Details: [Data visualization](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-data-visualization),
[Dashboards and summaries](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-dashboards-and-summaries).

## Lay out a page

| You need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| The root of a full-screen app | [Page](squonk-ui://components/page), once per screen |
| A bar across the top: brand, search, account | [Header](squonk-ui://components/header), or `StickyHeader` |
| Side navigation or a fixed panel | [Sidebar](squonk-ui://components/sidebar) |
| Panels people resize: list and detail, editor and preview | [ResizablePanels](squonk-ui://components/resizable-panels) |
| A band of a landing or content page | [Section](squonk-ui://components/section) with a [SectionHeading](squonk-ui://components/section-heading) |
| A readable width for content | [Container](squonk-ui://components/container) |
| A title on one side, actions on the other | [Split](squonk-ui://components/split) |
| Cards or figures in columns | [Grid](squonk-ui://components/grid) |
| Things in a column, or a row that wraps | [VStack](squonk-ui://components/vstack), [Cluster](squonk-ui://components/cluster) |
| A surface around one thing | [Card](squonk-ui://components/card) |
| A bounded area that scrolls | [ScrollBox](squonk-ui://components/scroll-box) |

Details: [Page layouts and app shells](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-page-layouts-and-app-shells),
[Space and layout](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-space-and-layout).

## Set the size and voice of a region

Use [Presentation](squonk-ui://components/presentation) (or a Section's or
Header's `register`) to size a region's controls for its job: `compact` for dense
work screens, `default` for most of an app, `large` and `hero` for landing pages.
Never size components one by one. Details:
[Density and registers](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-density-and-registers).

## Words, pictures and icons

| You need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| A page or section title | [Heading](squonk-ui://components/heading) at the right level |
| Body text, secondary text | [Text](squonk-ui://components/text) with `tone` |
| A symbol inside a control or a line of text | An [Icon](squonk-ui://components/icon) |
| A picture beside a message: an empty state, a finished step | An [Illustration](squonk-ui://components/illustration) |
| A keyboard shortcut, or code | [Kbd](squonk-ui://components/kbd), [Code](squonk-ui://components/code) |
| A formatted amount of money | [Currency](squonk-ui://components/currency) |

Details: [Illustrations, icons and images](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-illustrations-icons-and-images),
[Writing for the interface](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-writing-for-the-interface).

## When nothing fits

Compose before you build. Most "missing components" are a layout primitive
around existing components, a scoped theme change, or a register. If you still
need something new, describe the job, when to use it and when not to, its states
and its keyboard behaviour, and ask for it to join the library rather than
building a private copy.

guides.text:
# Dashboards and summaries An overview screen answers "what needs my attention, and how are things going?" in that order. It is usually the first page of an app, so it sets the tone: lead with what people must do, then the few figures they act on, then a way into the detail. Build it from [Alert](squonk-ui://components/alert), [Stat](squonk-ui://components/stat), [Card](squonk-ui://components/card), [Grid](squonk-ui://components/grid) and, where a trend matters, the charts. **Example:** What needs doing first, then three figures, then recent activity with a link to all of it. ```tsx export function OverviewScreenExample() { return ( Annual dues for the 2026–27 season are due 28 November. Pay now Recent activity See all
  • Payment of $1,240.00 received · 2 Nov
  • Swamp Fund levy paid for October · 1 Nov
    •      ); } // ---- Settings and preferences ------------------------------------------------- /** Settings grouped under headings: switches that save at once, and a group saved with its own button. */ ``` ## What goes where | Part | Use | Rules | | --- | --- | --- | | Something that needs action soon | An [Alert](squonk-ui://components/alert) at the top, with a link to do it | One or two. If everything is urgent, nothing is | | The figures people act on | A row of [Stat](squonk-ui://components/stat)s in a `Grid` of Cards | Three or four. Add `change` only when the comparison means something | | A trend behind a figure | Stat `trend`, a [Sparkline](squonk-ui://components/sparkline), or a chart in its own Card below | See [Data visualization](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-data-visualization) | | Recent activity | A short list in a Card, with "See all" | Five items or so; the full list lives on its own page | | Ways into common tasks | [InteractiveCard](squonk-ui://components/interactive-card)s or plain links | Only the tasks most people do most often | | A level against a limit | [Meter](squonk-ui://components/meter) | Say the level in words as well as colour | ## Summaries of one thing A summary page for one record (a membership account, a case, a member) follows the same order on a smaller scale: its status as a [Badge](squonk-ui://components/badge) next to its name, an Alert if something needs doing, the key figures, then details grouped under headings, often in [Tabs](squonk-ui://components/tabs) when the views are separate ("Summary", "Payments", "History"). ## Before a big action A review step before submitting ("Check your answers") is a summary too: group the answers under the same headings as the form, show each value as people will see it, and give each group a "Change" link back to the step. See [Multi-step forms](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-forms-multi-step-forms). ## Accessibility - Give the page one `h1`, and a heading for each card (`Heading level` to match the page's outline). Charts in cards set `hideTitle` so the heading isn't repeated. - Stat and Sparkline describe their figures and direction in words; don't add a second description. - An Alert that appears as the page loads isn't announced as news; that's intended. Don't move focus to it. - Keep the reading order the order of importance: attention, figures, detail. ## Pitfalls - **A wall of numbers.** Every figure should change what someone does. Leave the rest for a report. - **Status colours as decoration.** Green and red mean good and bad news; don't use them to tell figures apart. - **Stale figures without a date.** Say when the data was last updated if it isn't live. - **Empty dashboards on day one.** A new account has nothing to summarise yet; show set-up steps instead. See [Onboarding and first run](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-onboarding-and-first-run). The [Member dashboard] and [Sighting insights] examples show a member's overview and a chart-led report. ## Related - [Data visualization](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-data-visualization) - [Lists, tables and cards](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-lists-tables-and-cards) - [Page layouts and app shells](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-page-layouts-and-app-shells)

guides.text:
# Data visualization

Start from the question people are asking of the data, then pick the form that
answers it. Every chart in the library shares one frame: a required title, a
table view of the same data, a legend once there are two series, a tooltip you
can reach by keyboard, and one categorical palette. Your app owns the data, its
formatting and the words.

## Choosing a form

| The question | Use |
| --- | --- |
| How many, how much, right now? | [Stat](squonk-ui://components/stat). Sometimes the right chart is a number. |
| Which way has this figure been heading? | [Sparkline](squonk-ui://components/sparkline) beside the figure, or a Stat with `trend` |
| How did it change over time? | [LineChart](squonk-ui://components/line-chart); [AreaChart](squonk-ui://components/area-chart) when the total volume matters, stacked to show what it is made of |
| How do these categories compare? | [BarChart](squonk-ui://components/bar-chart); horizontal for a ranking or long category names |
| What is the whole made of? | [DonutChart](squonk-ui://components/donut-chart) for two to five parts; a BarChart for more, or when parts need comparing with each other |
| Do these two measures move together? | [ScatterChart](squonk-ui://components/scatter-chart) |
| How full is it, against a known limit? | [Meter](squonk-ui://components/meter) |
| How far along is this task? | [ProgressBar](squonk-ui://components/progress-bar). It tracks work toward done, not a measure, so it carries no warning levels. |
| How are these things connected to each other? | [NetworkGraph](squonk-ui://components/network-graph), for up to about 150 things linked many-to-many. To look one of them up, use a Table. |
| What exactly is the value for this row? | [Table](squonk-ui://components/table). If people will look values up, a chart is the wrong tool. |

A chart shows shape: rising, falling, bigger, smaller, clustered. If no one will
act on the shape, show the numbers.

## Every form, by example

One example of each, all from the same Squonk Society data, so you can compare
them side by side. Each component's own page covers its options.

### Figures and trends

[Stat](squonk-ui://components/stat) leads with the number;
[Sparkline](squonk-ui://components/sparkline) shows which way it has been
heading in the space of a word, beside a figure or in a table cell.

**Example:** A Stat with its change and trend; Sparklines beside the figures in a list of chapters.

```tsx
<Grid columns={{ mobile: 1, tablet: 2 }} gap="md">
  <Card>
    <Stat label="Members" value="2,418" change={0.034} changeLabel="vs last quarter" trend={[2210, 2264, 2301, 2338, 2392, 2418]} trendLabel="Members, last 6 quarters" />
  </Card>
  <Card>
    <VStack gap="sm">
      <Text variant="eyebrow">Sightings, last 12 weeks</Text>
      <HStack gap="md" align="center" justify="between">
        <Text>Auckland</Text>
        <HStack gap="sm" align="center">
          <Sparkline data={[120, 132, 128, 151, 149, 170, 168, 182, 195, 191, 214, 230]} label="Auckland sightings, last 12 weeks" slot={2} />
          <Text weight="bold">230</Text>
        </HStack>
      </HStack>
      <HStack gap="md" align="center" justify="between">
        <Text>Wellington</Text>
        <HStack gap="sm" align="center">
          <Sparkline data={[96, 92, 99, 94, 90, 88, 91, 85, 83, 86, 80, 78]} label="Wellington sightings, last 12 weeks" slot={2} />
          <Text weight="bold">78</Text>
        </HStack>
      </HStack>
    </VStack>
  </Card>
</Grid>
```

### Change over time

[LineChart](squonk-ui://components/line-chart) for how a figure moved;
[AreaChart](squonk-ui://components/area-chart) when the total matters too.
Stack the areas to show what the total is made of.

**Example:** Two series on one value axis, then the same kind of data stacked to show the total and its parts.

```tsx
<Grid columns={{ mobile: 1, desktop: 2 }} gap="md">
  <LineChart
    title="Night-watch turnout by month"
    description="Members attending, 2026"
    data={[
      { month: "Jun", auckland: 52, waikato: 31 },
      { month: "Jul", auckland: 58, waikato: 35 },
      { month: "Aug", auckland: 56, waikato: 40 },
      { month: "Sep", auckland: 63, waikato: 44 },
      { month: "Oct", auckland: 71, waikato: 49 },
    ]}
    xKey="month"
    xLabel="Month"
    series={[
      { key: "auckland", label: "Auckland" },
      { key: "waikato", label: "Waikato" },
    ]}
  />
  <AreaChart
    title="Sightings logged by channel"
    description="Sightings per week, first quarter"
    stacked
    data={[
      { week: "W1", online: 82, lead: 31, paper: 12 },
      { week: "W2", online: 90, lead: 29, paper: 11 },
      { week: "W3", online: 97, lead: 34, paper: 9 },
      { week: "W4", online: 104, lead: 33, paper: 8 },
      { week: "W5", online: 118, lead: 36, paper: 8 },
      { week: "W6", online: 126, lead: 38, paper: 6 },
    ]}
    xKey="week"
    xLabel="Week"
    series={[
      { key: "online", label: "Online" },
      { key: "lead", label: "Chapter lead" },
      { key: "paper", label: "Paper" },
    ]}
  />
</Grid>
```

### Comparing categories and parts of a whole

[BarChart](squonk-ui://components/bar-chart) compares categories;
[DonutChart](squonk-ui://components/donut-chart) shows the share of a
whole, for two to five parts.

**Example:** Grouped bars compare two seasons per chapter; the donut splits one month's dues by type.

```tsx
<Grid columns={{ mobile: 1, desktop: 2 }} gap="md">
  <BarChart
    title="Sightings by chapter"
    description="2025 and 2026 seasons"
    data={[
      { chapter: "Auckland", s2025: 431, s2026: 482 },
      { chapter: "Wellington", s2025: 240, s2026: 219 },
      { chapter: "Canterbury", s2025: 171, s2026: 198 },
      { chapter: "Waikato", s2025: 120, s2026: 143 },
    ]}
    xKey="chapter"
    xLabel="Chapter"
    series={[
      { key: "s2025", label: "2025" },
      { key: "s2026", label: "2026" },
    ]}
  />
  <DonutChart
    title="Dues collected by type"
    description="October 2026, NZD"
    data={[
      { type: "Annual dues", amount: 38400 },
      { type: "Swamp Fund levy", amount: 26100 },
      { type: "Night-watch kit hire", amount: 17900 },
      { type: "Field-trip deposit", amount: 4200 },
    ]}
    nameKey="type"
    valueKey="amount"
    nameLabel="Dues type"
    valueLabel="Collected"
    formatValue={(v) => `$${(v / 1000).toFixed(1)}K`}
  />
</Grid>
```

### Two measures together

[ScatterChart](squonk-ui://components/scatter-chart) plots one thing per
dot against two measures, to show whether they move together.

**Example:** Each dot is one membership: how late its dues are against how much is owed.

```tsx
<ScatterChart
  title="Overdue dues"
  description="Each dot is one membership"
  series={[
    {
      label: "Wanderers",
      data: [
        { name: "Aroha Ngata", daysLate: 4, owing: 50 },
        { name: "James Whitfield", daysLate: 12, owing: 120 },
        { name: "Mei Lin Chen", daysLate: 21, owing: 180 },
        { name: "Tama Rāwiri", daysLate: 33, owing: 310 },
        { name: "Sofia Petrov", daysLate: 45, owing: 390 },
      ],
    },
    {
      label: "Keepers",
      data: [
        { name: "Chen Household", daysLate: 8, owing: 240 },
        { name: "Olu Whānau", daysLate: 19, owing: 520 },
        { name: "Ngata Trust", daysLate: 30, owing: 760 },
        { name: "Harbour Keepers", daysLate: 52, owing: 1180 },
      ],
    },
  ]}
  xKey="daysLate"
  yKey="owing"
  nameKey="name"
  xLabel="Days late"
  yLabel="Dues owing"
  formatY={(v) => `$${v}`}
/>
```

### Against a limit, and toward done

[Meter](squonk-ui://components/meter) shows a measure against a known
limit, with warning and critical levels.
[ProgressBar](squonk-ui://components/progress-bar) shows a task moving
toward done. They look alike, so pick by what the bar means.

**Example:** The meter turns to warning past 48 GB; the progress bar has no levels, only how far the task has got.

```tsx
<Card>
  <VStack gap="lg">
    <Meter label="Field-photo storage" value={51} maxValue={60} valueLabel="51 of 60 GB" showValue warningAt={48} criticalAt={57} />
    <ProgressBar label="Importing the 2026 sighting log" value={64} showValue />
  </VStack>
</Card>
```

### Connections

[NetworkGraph](squonk-ui://components/network-graph) shows how things link
to each other, many-to-many: clusters, hubs and things that stand alone. Give it
a [NetworkGraphLegend](squonk-ui://components/network-graph) built from
the same `nodeKinds` and `linkKinds`, so the key always matches the drawing.
Shape, not only colour, tells the kinds apart.

**Example:** Who funds, leads and shares maps with each chapter. Select a node to see what it connects to.

```tsx
<VStack gap="sm">
  <NetworkGraphLegend nodeKinds={chapterNodeKinds} linkKinds={chapterLinkKinds} nodes={chapterNodes} links={chapterLinks} />
  <NetworkGraph
    label="Who funds, leads and shares maps with each chapter"
    style={{ height: 360 }}
    nodes={chapterNodes}
    links={chapterLinks}
    nodeKinds={chapterNodeKinds}
    linkKinds={chapterLinkKinds}
  />
</VStack>
```

### Exact values

[Table](squonk-ui://components/table) when people look values up, compare
them exactly or sort them. Every chart above already has a table view of its own
data; reach for a Table when the table is the point.

**Example:** The same chapters as the bar chart, as numbers to read and sort.

```tsx
<Table
  caption="Sightings by chapter, 2026 season"
  rowKey="chapter"
  columns={[
    { key: "chapter", header: "Chapter" },
    { key: "sightings", header: "Sightings", align: "right" },
    { key: "verified", header: "Verified", align: "right" },
  ]}
  rows={[
    { chapter: "Auckland", sightings: 482, verified: "93%" },
    { chapter: "Wellington", sightings: 219, verified: "90%" },
    { chapter: "Canterbury", sightings: 198, verified: "88%" },
    { chapter: "Waikato", sightings: 143, verified: "91%" },
  ]}
/>
```

## Colour

- Series take the eight palette slots (`--squonk-roles-color-data-series1`…`8`) **in
  order**. The order is fixed and checked for colour-vision deficiencies, so
  don't reorder it or pick colours by taste.
- Colour follows the series, never its position. When a series can be filtered
  out, or the same measure appears in several charts on a page, pin it with
  `slot` so it keeps its colour. A Sparkline or Stat trend that shows the same
  measure takes the same slot.
- Eight series is the most one chart colours apart. Before that, fold the small
  ones into "Other" (DonutChart does this past seven parts) or split the chart
  into small multiples.
- Status colours (success, warning, error) are reserved for good and bad news:
  Stat's change and Meter's levels. Don't use them as series colours.
- Text is never drawn in a series colour. Labels, legends and tooltips use text
  colours and a swatch beside them, so they stay readable for everyone.

## One axis per chart

Charts have one value axis. When two measures have different units or scales
(dues collected and the number of sightings, say), draw **two charts** side by
side with the same x axis, rather than one chart with an axis on each side. Dual
axes invite people to read meaning into where the lines cross, and that point
depends only on how the axes were scaled.

## Dashboards

Lead with a row of Stats in a [Grid](squonk-ui://components/grid) of
[Cards](squonk-ui://components/card): the three or four figures people act on.
Charts that explain them go below, each in its own Card. Give each card a
`Heading` at the right level for the page and set `hideTitle` on the chart, so the
heading isn't repeated; the chart's `title` still names it for screen readers and
captions its table view.

**Example:** Figures first, then a chart for each question. Each chart's card has a heading; the chart's own title is hidden but still names it.

```tsx
<VStack gap="md">
  <Grid columns={{ mobile: 1, tablet: 3 }} gap="md">
    <Card>
      <Stat label="Dues collected" value="$86.6K" change={0.052} changeLabel="vs October 2025" trend={[71, 74, 73, 78, 80, 79, 83, 86.6]} trendLabel="Dues collected, last 8 months" />
    </Card>
    <Card>
      <Stat label="Overdue dues" value="$4.2K" change={0.08} changeLabel="vs last quarter" increaseIs="bad" trend={[3.4, 3.6, 3.5, 3.9, 4.0, 4.2]} trendLabel="Overdue dues, last 6 quarters" trendSlot={2} />
    </Card>
    <Card>
      <Stat label="Sightings verified" value="91.2%" change={-0.004} changeLabel="vs last year" trend={[89, 90, 90.5, 91.6, 91.2]} trendLabel="Sightings verified, last 5 years" trendSlot={3} />
```

Keep a dashboard to the questions people bring to it. If a chart doesn't change
what anyone does, leave it out.

## Accessibility

- **Every chart has a title**, even when `hideTitle` hides it. It names the chart
  for assistive technology and captions the table view. Say what is shown and
  over what ("Sightings logged by chapter, 2026"), not "Chart".
- **Table view.** Every chart has a "Table view" toggle that shows the same data
  as a [Table](squonk-ui://components/table). It serves screen reader users,
  people who need exact values and anyone who can't separate the colours. Don't
  hide it, and don't build a second table beside the chart.
- **Keyboard.** Tab to the plot: focus shows the first point, and the left and
  right arrow keys move the tooltip from point to point, as hover does with a
  mouse. Horizontal bar charts aren't a focus stop, because the arrow keys
  can't step through them; there the table view is the keyboard route, as it
  is for exact values in every chart.
- **Legend.** A chart with two or more series shows a legend of swatches and
  names in text colour. Pair colour with something else where you can: direct
  labels, the order of the legend matching the order of the marks, or a split
  into separate charts.
- Sparkline and Stat speak their first and last values and the direction of
  change in words; Meter announces its `valueLabel`. Say warning and critical
  levels in words as well as colour.

guides.summary: A staff work queue and a public landing page need different sizes of the same controls. Set the size once, for a region, by its job: never component by component. The library gives you four registers through Presentation, and ThemeStyleBlock for a region that needs a denser or larger theme as a whole.
guides.text:
# Density and registers

A staff work queue and a public landing page need different sizes of the same
controls. Set the size once, for a region, by its job: never component by
component. The library gives you four registers through
[Presentation](squonk-ui://components/presentation), and
[ThemeStyleBlock](squonk-ui://components/theme-style-block) for a region that
needs a denser or larger theme as a whole.

**Example:** The same Select, Button and Badge in the compact and default registers. Heights, padding and text step together, so a row of mixed controls still lines up.

```tsx
export function RegistersExample() {
  return (
    <Grid columns={{ mobile: 1, tablet: 2 }} gap="lg">
      {(["compact", "default"] as const).map((register) => (
        <Presentation key={register} register={register}>
          <VStack gap="sm">
            <Text weight="bold">{register}</Text>
            <Select label="Status" defaultValue="open" options={[{ value: "open", label: "Open" }, { value: "closed", label: "Closed" }]} />
            <Cluster gap="sm" align="center">
              <Button variant="primary">Assign</Button>
              <Badge tone="info">12 cases</Badge>
            </Cluster>
          </VStack>
        </Presentation>
      ))}
    </Grid>
  );
}
```

## Choosing a register

| The region is… | Register | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A dense work screen used all day, mostly with a mouse | `compact` | Staff queues, admin tables, toolbars, filter panels |
| Most of an app | `default` | Forms, dashboards, settings, account pages |
| A display band that needs more weight than an app page | `large` | Landing page features, a summary band |
| The headline of a landing page | `hero` | The first Section of a marketing page |

Start with `default`. Move to `compact` only when people need to see more at
once and will use a pointer; touch users need the default sizes.

## How to set it

| You want | Use |
| --- | --- |
| A register for a region of the page | `<Presentation register="compact">` around it |
| A band of a landing page with its own register | [Section](squonk-ui://components/section) `register="hero"`; it sets the register for everything inside |
| A header with a different register from the page | [Header](squonk-ui://components/header) `register` |
| A region whose whole theme (spacing, type and radius) scales down or up | [ThemeStyleBlock](squonk-ui://components/theme-style-block) `register="compact"` or `"display"` |
| A specific value changed for part of a page | [ThemeModifier](squonk-ui://components/theme-modifier) |

`Presentation` picks control sizes from the theme without changing it.
`ThemeStyleBlock` rebuilds the theme for its subtree from scaled primitives, so
space and type between components change too. Use Presentation first; reach for
ThemeStyleBlock when a whole region needs to feel denser, not only its controls.
See [Theme](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-theme).

## Rules

- **Choose by region, not by component.** No component has its own size prop;
  wrap the region instead. A button that needs to be bigger than its neighbours
  usually needs to be `primary`, not larger.
- **Nest to change it.** A default-sized card inside a hero section nests its
  own `Presentation register="default"`.
- **Keep one register per task.** A form that mixes compact and default fields
  looks broken.
- **Don't shrink the whole app** to fit one dense table. Make the table's region
  compact and leave the rest.

## Accessibility

- Compact controls are smaller targets. Keep them for pointer-heavy screens, and
  check that they still meet the minimum target size you support.
- Registers change size, not contrast or focus: focus rings and text contrast
  stay the same in every register.
- Check the page zoomed to 200% in each register you use.

## Pitfalls

- **Per-component overrides** with `style` or CSS to change a size. They break
  alignment with neighbouring controls and drift from the theme.
- **`hero` in an app.** It's for marketing headlines, not page titles.
- **Compact on phones.** Small targets and small text on a small screen are hard
  to use.

## Related

- [Space and layout](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-space-and-layout)
- [Theme](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-theme)
- [Page layouts and app shells](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-page-layouts-and-app-shells)

guides.summary: Most of what we build is forms, so every form works the same way. Three layers, each doing one job:
guides.text:
# Forms

Most of what we build is forms, so every form works the same way. Three layers,
each doing one job:

| Layer | Does | Comes from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Fields** | Labels, help and error text wired to the input, keyboard behaviour, focus, the look | Library components on [React Aria](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/) |
| **Form state** | Values, which fields were touched, running validators, submitting | [TanStack Form](https://tanstack.com/form), through `useAppForm` |
| **Rules** | What counts as valid, and the message when it isn't | A [Zod](https://zod.dev) schema (any [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev) library works) |

`useAppForm` from `@squonkstack/ui/form` joins them: its fields are the library's
fields, already bound to the value, blur state and error.

## How every form behaves

- **Errors wait.** A field's error shows once it has been left or a submit has
  been tried, never while someone is typing it the first time. After that it
  updates live as they fix it.
- **A failed submit says everything at once.** The error summary appears at the
  top, takes focus, and links each message to its field.
- **The submit button stays enabled.** A disabled button can't explain what's
  wrong. While a submit runs it is marked busy and ignores presses.
- **The server's errors look like ours.** Errors from the API land on their
  field and in the summary.

## Where to start

| You need | Read |
| --- | --- |
| A form with a few fields | [The basics](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-forms-the-basics) |
| Fields that must agree, or a check against the server | [Validation](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-forms-validation) |
| To show the API's errors | [Server errors](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-forms-server-errors) |
| Questions that depend on answers, or lists people add to | [Conditional and repeating fields](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-forms-conditional-and-repeating-fields) |
| A long form split into steps | [Multi-step forms](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-forms-multi-step-forms) |
| A field the library doesn't have | [Custom fields](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-forms-custom-fields) |

## Why this stack

**React Aria for fields.** It is the base of every component in this library.
Each field gets the label, description and error relationships, `aria-invalid`,
and the keyboard behaviour of the WAI-ARIA patterns without us maintaining them.

**TanStack Form for state.** React Aria handles a field; it doesn't manage a
form. Its own `Form` sets how validation behaves and can display server errors,
but it doesn't hold values, track what was touched, compare fields, run async
checks, manage repeating groups or track submission. TanStack Form does all of
that, headless, so it sits behind our fields without changing how they look. Field
names are type-checked against `defaultValues`, and it takes any Standard
Schema validator.

We looked at React Hook Form, the other common choice. It works with React Aria
too, but it is built around uncontrolled inputs registered by ref, and React
Aria's fields are controlled components, so every field would go through
`Controller`. TanStack Form is controlled by design, so React Aria's fields bind
to it directly.

**Zod for rules.** One schema gives the types and the messages, and the same
schema can run on the server.

## Rules for writing forms

- Give every field a visible label. A placeholder is not a label.
- Write messages that make sense on their own, because they also appear in the
  error summary: "Enter your full name", not "Required".
- Ask only what you need, and say why when it isn't obvious.
- Put the error summary at the top of every form longer than a couple of fields.

See also [Labels, help and validation](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-labels-help-and-validation)
and the [Form](squonk-ui://components/form) reference.

guides.title: Labels: Badge or Tag
guides.summary: Both are small labels, so they are easy to confuse. They answer different questions, and people learn to read them differently, so keep them apart.
guides.text:
# Labels: Badge or Tag Both are small labels, so they are easy to confuse. They answer different questions, and people learn to read them differently, so keep them apart. **A Badge reports. A Tag names.** ```tsx
Status: Overdue Paid 3 {}}>Night watches {}}>Waikato Chapter
``` | | Badge | Tag | | --- | --- | --- | | What it is | The state or count of the thing beside it | A value: a category, keyword, chosen filter or entered item | | Who sets it | The system. It changes on its own (Overdue → Paid) | The person: added, chosen or removed. Or it names what something is | | Interactive? | Never | Can be removed; in a `TagGroup` it is one tab stop with arrow keys between tags | | Colour means | Meaning: success, warning, error, info | Grouping only (`neutral`, `primary`, `info`), never status | | Shape | Pill, read as a marker | Chip with squarer corners, read as an object you hold | ## The test - Is it something the person picked, or a name for what it is? Use a **Tag**. - Is it reporting how something stands, or how many? Use a **Badge**. | Example | Use | | --- | --- | | "Overdue", "In progress", "Paid", "Beta" | Badge | | "3" new notifications, a count on a Filters button | Badge | | An applied filter "Night watches ×", email recipients in a field | Tag | | A read-only category on a record ("Night watches", "Waikato Chapter") | Tag: it names what the record is and doesn't change on its own | | A sentence such as "Includes about $4 late fee" | Neither: that is supporting text | ## Common mistakes - **A red Tag.** Colour on a label reads as status. Tags have no success, warning or error tones for this reason; if it is a status, it is a Badge. - **A Badge with a remove button.** People can't remove a status. If they can remove it, it is a value: a Tag. - **A sentence in a Badge.** Badges are one or two words or a number. Longer notes are text beside the content. - **Making either one the only signal.** Colour supports the words; the text must say the status or value on its own. **Do:** One or two words that report a state. ```tsx Overdue Paid ``` **Don't:** A sentence in a badge. Longer notes are text beside the content. ```tsx Includes about $4 late fee added to what's left ``` ## People and identity Compose [Avatar](squonk-ui://components/avatar), [MediaObject](squonk-ui://components/media-object), Text and a Badge for a person or a resource. Initials stand in when there's no image; they identify someone visually but say nothing about who is signed in or online. Give an informative image a text alternative, and hide it when the name beside it already says who it is. Long names and missing images must keep the row's layout. **Example:** An image or initials, a name, a role, and availability in words that survive without colour. ```tsx export function IdentityExample() { return ( {[ { name: "Hana Walker", role: "Membership officer, Wellington Chapter", status: "Available", tone: "success" as const }, { name: "Sam Patel", role: "Chapter lead, Dues and member cases, Auckland Chapter", status: "Away until Monday", tone: "warning" as const }, ].map((person) => ( } align="center"> {person.name} {person.status} {person.role} ))} ); } ``` See [Badge](squonk-ui://components/badge) and [Tag](squonk-ui://components/tag).

guides.title: Labels, help and validation
guides.summary: Give every TextField, Select, Checkbox and RadioGroup a visible `label` (or `legend`). A placeholder is not a label: it disappears as soon as someone types. Use `aria-label` only when the purpose is already visible some other way, such as a search field next to a "Search" button.
guides.text:
# Labels, help and validation

## Label every field visibly

Give every [TextField](squonk-ui://components/text-field),
[Select](squonk-ui://components/select), [Checkbox](squonk-ui://components/checkbox)
and [RadioGroup](squonk-ui://components/radio) a visible `label` (or `legend`).
A placeholder is not a label: it disappears as soon as someone types. Use
`aria-label` only when the purpose is already visible some other way, such as a
search field next to a "Search" button.

**Do:** Visible labels, help that explains the format, and an error that says what to do.

```tsx
export function LabelledFieldExample() {
  return (
    <VStack gap="md">
      <TextField label="Membership number" helperText="Starts with SQ, on your membership card." />
      <TextField label="First payment" type="date" error="Enter a date after today" />
    </VStack>
  );
}

/** A placeholder standing in for a label, and an error that doesn't help. */
```

**Don't:** Placeholders vanish as people type, and “Invalid input” doesn't say how to fix it.

```tsx
export function PlaceholderFieldExample() {
  return (
    <VStack gap="md">
      <TextField aria-label="Membership number" placeholder="Membership number" />
      <TextField aria-label="First payment" placeholder="First payment" error="Invalid input" />
    </VStack>
  );
}

// ---- Overlays and disclosures -------------------------------------------------

/** The lightest surface first: inline disclosure, then a popover, then a modal. */
```

## Help text explains the format, not the error

`helperText` sits under the field and is read with it. Use it for format and
constraints ("8 or more characters"). When there is an error, the `error` message
replaces it and the field is marked invalid.

## When to show errors

- **Not while someone is still typing.** Show a field's error after they leave it
  or when they submit, so half-typed values aren't called wrong.
- **Live checking only helps when it guides typing**, such as password rules shown
  as a checklist.
- **On submit,** keep every value, mark each invalid field, and move focus once:
  to an error summary listing the problems as links when there are several, or to
  the first invalid field.
- **Server errors** belong on the field they concern and clear when the user
  edits it.

[Form](squonk-ui://components/form) (`@squonkstack/ui/form`) does all of this:
errors after blur or submit, the error summary with focus and links, and server
errors mapped onto their fields. The [Forms](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-forms-overview)
section shows each case working.

Write errors as instructions: "Enter a date after today", not "Invalid input".

## Required and optional

Mark whichever is rarer. Most of our forms are mostly required, so mark the
optional fields ("(optional)" in the label) and say so once at the top. The
sources we checked don't settle this; it is our convention. Always set
`required` on the field as well, so assistive technology announces it.

## Related

- [Toasts, alerts and dialogs](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-toasts-alerts-and-dialogs) — a toast never replaces a field error
- [Forms](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-forms-overview): state, validation, server errors and steps

---

[Form](https://react-aria.adobe.com/Form), [React Spectrum forms](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/forms), © Adobe;
[React Aria forms guide](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/forms.html);
[WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/), © W3C, under the
[W3C Software and Document License](https://www.w3.org/copyright/software-license/).

guides.title: Lists, tables and cards
guides.summary: The same records can be shown as a table, a list or a grid of cards. Choose by what people do with them: compare, read in order, or pick one to open. How many there are matters less.
guides.text:
# Lists, tables and cards The same records can be shown as a table, a list or a grid of cards. Choose by what people do with them: compare, read in order, or pick one to open. How many there are matters less. ## Choosing a form | People will… | Use | Why | | --- | --- | --- | | Compare values across items, sort, or select rows to act on | [Table](squonk-ui://components/table) | Columns line values up; headers sort; rows select | | Read items one after another: messages, activity, results | A list: `VStack as="ul"` with a [MediaObject](squonk-ui://components/media-object) per item | One line per item, easy to scan top to bottom | | Choose one of a few items, each with its own page | A [Grid](squonk-ui://components/grid) of [InteractiveCard](squonk-ui://components/interactive-card)s | Each card is one big target with room for a summary | | See a few items, each with several actions | A Grid of [Card](squonk-ui://components/card)s with real buttons | A whole-card link can't hold other controls | | Skim a feed once, newest first, that keeps growing | [InfiniteList](squonk-ui://components/infinite-list) | Loads more as people scroll; the feed pattern lets keyboards skip it | | Read a short set of label and value pairs about one thing | A two-column list, or a Table without sorting | Labels and values line up | ## Tables compare **Example:** A table: values in columns, a sortable header, statuses as badges. ```tsx export function ReadingTableExample() { return ; } /** A selectable grid: one tab stop, rows chosen to act on. */ ``` Use a table when the columns mean the same thing on every row and people read across them. Keep a column to one kind of value, align numbers on the right, and give the table a `caption`. On phones a table scrolls sideways inside its own area; if most columns don't matter on a phone, show fewer or switch to a list. See [Tables and grids](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-tables-and-grids). ## Lists read in order **Example:** A list: one line per item, the title as the link, details in secondary text. ```tsx export function SimpleListExample() { return ( {LETTERS.map((letter, i) => (
  • {i > 0 ? : null} } align="center"> {letter.title} {letter.from} · {letter.when}
    • ))}     ); } const LETTERS = [ { title: "Your sighting report was received", from: "Hana Walker", when: "Today" }, { title: "Reminder: Swamp Fund levy due 20 November", from: "Sam Patel", when: "Yesterday" }, { title: "Instalment plan approved", from: "Hana Walker", when: "3 Nov" }, ]; /** Cards: a few items people choose between, each with one destination. */ ``` Use a list when each item is mostly one line of text: a title, who and when. Render real list markup (`as="ul"`) so screen readers say how many items there are. Make the title the link, and keep any other action at the end of the row. Divide items with space or a [Divider](squonk-ui://components/divider), not boxes. ## Cards choose **Example:** Cards: a few items with one destination each. The whole card is the link. ```tsx export function CardGridExample() { return ( {[ { title: "Annual dues", detail: "Next payment due 28 November", status: Due soon }, { title: "Swamp Fund levy", detail: "Paid for October", status: Up to date }, { title: "Field-trip deposit", detail: "2026 deposit not started", status: Not started }, ].map((item) => ( {item.title} {item.detail}
    {item.status}
         ))}     ); } // ---- Dashboards and summaries ------------------------------------------------- /** An overview: what needs doing first, the figures people act on, then recent activity. */ ``` Use cards for a handful of items people pick between, each with a short summary or a status. Put the same information in the same order in every card. Use `Grid minColumnWidth` so cards wrap to fit the space. A grid of forty cards is a table or a list in disguise. See [Cards and landing sections](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-cards-and-landing-sections). ## More than one page of items - **Pages** (Table `pageSize`, or [Pagination](squonk-ui://components/pagination) for lists and cards) for records people come back to and refer to. - **Load more as people scroll** ([InfiniteList](squonk-ui://components/infinite-list)) for feeds read once. - **Search and filters** above any of them once there are more items than fit on a screen. See [Search, filtering and sorting](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-search-filtering-and-sorting). ## Accessibility - Tables need a `caption` and real column headers; lists need list markup. - An InteractiveCard's heading names it; never nest buttons or links inside one. - Keep one tab stop per item where you can: the item's link. Selecting rows is the Table's grid mode, not checkboxes in a list. - Statuses in any form say their meaning in words, not colour alone. ## Pitfalls - **Cards for data.** If people compare figures across cards, they want a table. - **A table for prose.** Rows of long sentences read better as a list. - **Mixed forms for the same records** on different screens. Pick one per kind of record and keep it. - **Each item a different shape.** Whatever the form, every item shows the same fields in the same place. ## Related - [Tables and grids](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-tables-and-grids) - [Empty and error states](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-empty-and-error-states) - [Choosing components](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-choosing-components)

guides.title: Loading and progress
guides.summary: Waiting is part of every screen. Show the wait in the place it affects, with what you actually know about it, and keep everything else usable. Choose from Skeleton, Spinner, ProgressBar and a Button's `pending` state.
guides.text:
# Loading and progress Waiting is part of every screen. Show the wait in the place it affects, with what you actually know about it, and keep everything else usable. Choose from [Skeleton](squonk-ui://components/skeleton), [Spinner](squonk-ui://components/spinner), [ProgressBar](squonk-ui://components/progress-bar) and a [Button](squonk-ui://components/button)'s `pending` state. ## Choosing an indicator | You know… | Use | Where | | --- | --- | --- | | The shape of what's coming (a table, a card, a paragraph) | [Skeleton](squonk-ui://components/skeleton) in that shape | In place of the content, so nothing jumps when it arrives | | Nothing about how long, and it should be short | [Spinner](squonk-ui://components/spinner) with a `label` that names the work | Where the result will appear | | How much is done (an upload, an import) | [ProgressBar](squonk-ui://components/progress-bar) with a `value` and `label` | Where the work was started | | It started from a button (save, submit, file) | The Button's `pending` | On the button itself | | It takes minutes or runs in the background | A status in the page and a toast when it's done | The page, and wherever people are when it finishes | **Example:** A skeleton for a known shape, a spinner for a short wait, and a bar for work you can measure. ```tsx export function LoadingExample() { const [progress, setProgress] = React.useState(40); return ( Known shape A short wait
); } // ---- Tables and grids --------------------------------------------------------- interface SightingRow { id: string; date: string; chapter: string; volume: string; status: "Verified" | "Under review" } const SIGHTING_ROWS: SightingRow[] = [ { id: "r1", date: "12 Sep 2026", chapter: "Waikato", volume: "340 mL", status: "Under review" }, { id: "r2", date: "3 Sep 2026", chapter: "Waikato", volume: "120 mL", status: "Verified" }, { id: "r3", date: "28 Aug 2026", chapter: "Taranaki", volume: "410 mL", status: "Verified" }, ]; const sightingColumns = [ { key: "date" as const, header: "Date", sortable: true }, { key: "chapter" as const, header: "Chapter" }, { key: "volume" as const, header: "Tear volume", align: "right" as const }, { key: "status", header: "Status", render: (row: SightingRow) => {row.status}, sortValue: (row: SightingRow) => row.status }, ]; /** A reading table: caption, sortable header, status badges. */ ``` ## Buttons that are working **Example:** The button keeps its label and its place in the tab order, says it's busy, and ignores presses until done. ```tsx export function PendingButtonExample() { const [pending, setPending] = React.useState(false); const [status, setStatus] = React.useState(""); return ( {status} ); } // ---- Illustrations, icons and images ------------------------------------------- /** An icon inside a control, an illustration beside a message. */ ``` Set `pending` while the action runs. Don't disable the button or replace its label with a spinner: people lose their place and screen readers lose the name. A form built with `useAppForm` gets this from `form.SubmitButton`, which can also show a `pendingLabel` in words, such as "Checking…". ## By how long it takes | Wait | Show | | --- | --- | | Under about a second | Nothing new. A flash of a spinner reads as a glitch | | A few seconds | A Skeleton or Spinner where the result goes, or `pending` on the button | | Longer, measurable | A ProgressBar with words ("Uploading 3 of 8 statements") | | Minutes, or work that continues if people leave | Say it's started, let them carry on, and notify when it finishes | These thresholds are our rule of thumb, not a standard. ## Refreshing and loading more - **Keep what's on screen** while it refreshes. Don't swap a populated table for skeletons; mark it as updating instead. - **Load more in place.** New rows join the end without moving focus; [InfiniteList](squonk-ui://components/infinite-list) handles this for feeds. - **Don't move focus** when data arrives. ## When it fails or takes too long - Replace the indicator with what happened and a way forward: "We couldn't load your sightings. Try again." See [Empty and error states](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-empty-and-error-states). - If a wait runs much longer than usual, say so and offer to keep waiting or cancel. - After a failed save, keep what people entered. ## Accessibility - Spinner and ProgressBar announce their `label`; make it say what's happening, not "Loading". - Skeletons are hidden from assistive technology. Mark the region that's loading with `aria-busy`, and announce when the content is ready if people are waiting for it. - Animations respect the motion level: indicators keep working without motion. ## Pitfalls - **Invented progress.** Never show a percentage for work you can't measure. - **A full-page spinner** for something that affects one card. - **Blocking the page** with a modal while something loads. - **A toast as the only sign** that long work finished: keep the result in the page too. ## Related - [Toasts, alerts and dialogs](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-toasts-alerts-and-dialogs) - [Empty and error states](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-empty-and-error-states) - [Tables and grids](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-tables-and-grids)

guides.title: Onboarding and first run
guides.summary: The first visit is the screen with the least in it and the most riding on it. Don't explain the app; get people to the first useful thing. Show what will appear and offer the first step, then step out of the way. Compose EmptyState, Illustration, ProgressBar, Card and Button.
guides.text:
# Onboarding and first run The first visit is the screen with the least in it and the most riding on it. Don't explain the app; get people to the first useful thing. Show what will appear and offer the first step, then step out of the way. Compose [EmptyState](squonk-ui://components/empty-state), [Illustration](squonk-ui://components/illustration), [ProgressBar](squonk-ui://components/progress-bar), [Card](squonk-ui://components/card) and [Button](squonk-ui://components/button). ## Which approach | The situation | Use | | --- | --- | | An area that's empty until people add something | A first-use [EmptyState](squonk-ui://components/empty-state): what will appear here, and one primary action to start | | Several set-up steps people can do in any order, over days | A set-up checklist in a Card on the overview, with progress | | Steps that must happen in order before the app works | A short [multi-step form](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-forms-multi-step-forms), then the app | | A new feature in an app people already know | An inline [Alert](squonk-ui://components/alert) `tone="info"` they can dismiss (`onDismiss`), next to the feature | | A term or field people may not understand | `helperText`, or a [Popover](squonk-ui://components/popover) with a link to more | ## First use **Example:** A first-use empty state: an illustration, what will appear here, and the first step. ```tsx export function FirstRunExample() { return ( } title="No sightings yet" body="Sightings you log appear here, with their verification status." action={} /> ); } // ---- Loading and progress ----------------------------------------------------- /** A button that shows it's working: it keeps its label and place, and ignores presses until done. */ ``` A first-use empty state says what the area is for and offers one way to start. An [Illustration](squonk-ui://components/illustration) makes the moment friendlier; leave it out in small spaces. Make the action specific ("Log your first sighting", not "Get started"). See [Empty and error states](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-empty-and-error-states). ## Set-up checklists **Example:** Progress in words and a bar, done steps marked, and the next step as the one primary action. ```tsx export function SetupChecklistExample() { const [done, setDone] = React.useState(["member", "bank"]); const next = SETUP_STEPS.find((s) => !done.includes(s.id)); return ( Finish setting up {SETUP_STEPS.map((step) => (
  • {done.includes(step.id) ? : null} {step.label}
    • ))}     {next ? (
    ) : ( You're all set. )}     ); } const SETUP_STEPS = [ { id: "member", label: "Add your member details", action: "Add member details" }, { id: "bank", label: "Add a bank account", action: "Add a bank account" }, { id: "chapter", label: "Choose your chapter", action: "Choose a chapter" }, { id: "household", label: "Invite your household", action: "Invite your household" }, ]; /** The first visit to an empty area: an illustration, what will appear here, and the first step. */ ``` - **Say how far along people are** in words ("2 of 4 done") as well as the bar. - **Offer the next step** as the one primary action; the rest stay in the list. - **Let people leave and come back.** Keep progress on the server, not in the browser. - **Go away when it's done.** Thank them once, then remove the checklist. ## Tours and walkthroughs The library has no tour or coach-mark component, on purpose. Overlays that point at parts of the screen hide what they explain, are hard to use with a keyboard or a screen reader, and are usually skipped. Put the explanation where it's needed: a clear label, help text, an empty state that teaches by doing. ## Accessibility - A checklist is an ordered list (`
      `); mark done steps with text or an icon with a `label`, not with colour or strikethrough alone. - Don't move focus to welcome messages or dismissible Alerts on load. - A dismissed message stays dismissed: remember it on the server. ## Pitfalls - **A welcome modal before anything else.** It blocks the first task to talk about it. - **Empty dashboards.** A new account's overview shows set-up, not zeros. - **Asking for everything up front.** Ask only what the first task needs; the rest can wait until it matters. - **Onboarding that never ends.** Every hint has an end: when it's done, or when it's dismissed. ## Related - [Empty and error states](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-empty-and-error-states) - [Dashboards and summaries](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-dashboards-and-summaries) - [Illustrations, icons and images](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-illustrations-icons-and-images)

guides.title: Overlays and disclosures
guides.summary: Pick the lightest surface that does the job. Each step up interrupts more and costs keyboard and screen-reader users more effort.
guides.text:
# Overlays and disclosures

Pick the lightest surface that does the job. Each step up interrupts more and
costs keyboard and screen-reader users more effort.

| You need to… | Use | In `@squonkstack/ui` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Show or hide a section in place (an FAQ answer, advanced settings) | An inline disclosure: a button with `aria-expanded` that reveals content below it | [Accordion](squonk-ui://components/accordion), with one item for a single disclosure |
| Offer a short list of commands for an item | A menu button | [DropdownMenu](squonk-ui://components/dropdown-menu) |
| Pick a value from a list | A select | [Select](squonk-ui://components/select) |
| Show a little content next to a control, with links or a few fields, without blocking the page | A non-modal dialog | [Popover](squonk-ui://components/popover) |
| Ask for a decision or a short task that must finish before continuing | A modal dialog | [Modal](squonk-ui://components/modal), [ConfirmModal](squonk-ui://components/modal) |
| A longer side task while keeping the page in view | A modal dialog at the edge of the screen | [Drawer](squonk-ui://components/drawer) |
| Name an icon-only control, or explain a term in a few words | A tooltip | [Tooltip](squonk-ui://components/tooltip); [IconButton](squonk-ui://components/icon-button) shows its label as one |

**Example:** From lightest to heaviest: an inline disclosure, a popover with a link, a tooltip naming an icon button, and a modal for a short task.

```tsx
export function OverlayLadderExample() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
  return (
    <VStack gap="lg">
      <Accordion
        items={[{ value: "late", title: "What happens if I log a sighting late?", content: <Text>You can still log it, but sightings more than 14 days old may need extra verification. Talk to us if you need a hand.</Text> }]}
      />
      <Cluster gap="sm" align="center">
        <Popover
          title="Tear volume"
          trigger={<Button variant="secondary">What counts as tear volume?</Button>}
          footer={<Link href="#tear-volume">More about measuring tear pools</Link>}
        >
          <Text>The estimated amount of tears in a pool, in millilitres, such as 250 mL.</Text>
        </Popover>
        <Tooltip content="Search sightings">
          <IconButton icon={<SearchIcon />} label="Search sightings" tooltip={false} />
        </Tooltip>
        <Button variant="primary" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Change bank account</Button>
      </Cluster>
      <Modal
        open={open}
        onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
        title="Change bank account"
        footer={<Cluster gap="sm"><Button variant="primary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Save</Button><Button variant="ghost" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button></Cluster>}
      >
        <TextField label="Account number" helperText="For example, 12-3456-7890123-00" />
      </Modal>
    </VStack>
  );
}

/** Information needed to use a field, hidden in a tooltip. */
```

## Inline disclosure first

If the extra content belongs to the page and the user may want it next to
everything else, reveal it in place. Nothing is hidden behind a layer, the page
keeps its scroll position, and the content is part of the normal reading order.
Keep interactive elements out of the disclosure button itself; put related
actions next to it.

## Menus are for actions, not values

`DropdownMenu` lists things to *do*. It has no value of its own and closes after
a choice. Use `Select` when the user is choosing a *value* that the form or page
keeps. Don't use a menu for site navigation: menu semantics promise app-like
keyboard behaviour that ordinary links don't need.

## Modal only when the page must wait

A `Modal` makes the rest of the page inert and hidden from assistive technology
until it closes, so use it only when the user genuinely can't continue without
answering. Give it a visible title (`title`) or an `aria-label`, keep a visible
way out (`onClose` shows the × button; Escape also asks to close), and keep the
content short. For long forms or multi-step work, use a page.

When content must float without blocking the page (an explanation with a link,
a few filters), use a `Popover`: it closes when people click elsewhere, so never
put anything they must finish in one. For longer side tasks use a `Drawer`, which
blocks the page like a `Modal` but keeps it in view.

## Tooltips are supplementary

Hover-only content is invisible to touch users and easy to miss with a magnifier.
If information is needed to use a control, show it as `helperText` on the field
instead. Never put links or buttons in a tooltip; content that needs interaction
needs a dialog or disclosure.

**Do:** The format is help text: always visible, and read with the field.

```tsx
export function HelpAsTextExample() {
  return <TextField label="Account number" helperText="Format: 12-3456-7890123-00" />;
}

// ---- Destructive actions ------------------------------------------------------

/** Remove at once and offer undo; confirm only what can't be undone. */
```

**Don't:** The format hidden in a tooltip: touch users never see it.

```tsx
export function HelpInTooltipExample() {
  return (
    <Cluster gap="xs" align="end">
      <TextField label="Account number" />
      <Tooltip content="Format: 12-3456-7890123-00">
        <IconButton icon={<InfoIcon />} label="Account number format" tooltip={false} />
      </Tooltip>
    </Cluster>
  );
}

/** The same information as help text, always visible. */
```

## Related

- [Focus management](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-focus-management)
- [Destructive actions](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-destructive-actions)
- [Menus and commands](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-menus-and-commands)

---

Sources, paraphrased: [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: dialog (modal)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/),
[disclosure](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/),
[menu button](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/) and
[tooltip](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tooltip/), © W3C, under the
[W3C Software and Document License](https://www.w3.org/copyright/software-license/);
[React Spectrum Tooltip and ContextualHelp guidance](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/v3/Tooltip.html), © Adobe;
[Chakra UI v3 Dialog](https://chakra-ui.com/docs/components/dialog) and
[Hover Card](https://chakra-ui.com/docs/components/hover-card) notes (MIT).
