guides.text:
# Patterns

Patterns are the decisions that sit above a single component: which control to
use, how a message should reach someone, what an empty screen should say. Each
page states the rule, shows it with real components, and says what your app
still owns.

## Start here

| Pattern | When you need it | Uses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Choosing components](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-choosing-components) | Which component to use for a job: act, ask, show a status, give feedback, wait, navigate, show data, lay out a page | Every component |
| [Page layouts and app shells](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-page-layouts-and-app-shells) | The shape of a screen, resizable workspaces, and how it responds across breakpoints | Page, Header, Sidebar, NavList, Section, Container, Grid, Split, ResizablePanels |
| [Writing for the interface](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-writing-for-the-interface) | Words for labels, buttons, errors, empty states and messages | Every component |
| [Density and registers](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-density-and-registers) | Sizing a region for its job, from dense admin to landing page | Presentation, Section, ThemeStyleBlock |

## Forms and input

| Pattern | When you need it | Uses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Forms](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-forms-overview) | Any form: state, validation, the error summary, server errors, steps | Form, every field |
| [Labels, help and validation](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-labels-help-and-validation) | Labelling a field, writing help text and errors | TextField, Select, Checkbox, RadioGroup |
| [Switches, checkboxes and saving](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-switches-checkboxes-and-saving) | A setting that saves at once, or a choice submitted later | Switch, Checkbox |
| [Choosing a selection control](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-choosing-a-selection-control) | One choice, several choices, or a long list | RadioGroup, Select, CheckboxGroup, Checkbox, Switch |
| [Settings and preferences](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-settings-and-preferences) | A settings page: grouping, saving at once or with a button, risky settings | Switch, RadioGroup, Fieldset, Button, ConfirmModal |

## Labels and surfaces

| Pattern | When you need it | Uses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Labels: Badge or Tag](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-labels-badge-or-tag) | A status, a count, a category or a person | Badge, Tag, Avatar, MediaObject |
| [Cards and landing sections](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-cards-and-landing-sections) | A card that links somewhere, a card with actions, comparable plans | Card, InteractiveCard, Section, Grid |
| [Illustrations, icons and images](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-illustrations-icons-and-images) | An icon, an illustration or a photograph: which, where and how big | Icon, Illustration, Avatar, AspectRatio |

## Feedback

| Pattern | When you need it | Uses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Toasts, alerts and dialogs](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-toasts-alerts-and-dialogs) | Telling someone something happened, or is happening | Toast, Alert, ConfirmModal |
| [Loading and progress](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-loading-and-progress) | Waiting for data or work: which indicator, where, and for how long | Skeleton, Spinner, ProgressBar, Button |
| [Empty and error states](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-empty-and-error-states) | Nothing to show yet, no matches, or a failed load | EmptyState, Button |
| [Onboarding and first run](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-onboarding-and-first-run) | A first visit, a set-up checklist, a new feature | EmptyState, Illustration, ProgressBar, Alert |
| [Destructive actions](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-destructive-actions) | Deleting or closing something | ConfirmModal, Toast, DropdownMenu |

## Overlays

| Pattern | When you need it | Uses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Overlays and disclosures](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-overlays-and-disclosures) | Showing more without leaving the page | Accordion, Popover, Tooltip, Modal, Drawer |
| [Menus and commands](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-menus-and-commands) | A short list of things to do with an item | DropdownMenu, IconButton |
| [Focus management](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-focus-management) | Anything that opens, closes, appears or disappears | Modal, DropdownMenu, Table |

## Navigation

| Pattern | When you need it | Uses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [App navigation](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-app-navigation) | The frame around a signed-in app | Header, Sidebar, NavList, Breadcrumb, Tabs, Link |
| [QR handoff](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-qr-handoff) | Moving someone from a screen to their phone | QrCode, Link |
| [Printing](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-printing) | A page people print: a statement, receipt or plan | Printable, NotPrintable, PrintOnly |

## Data and content

| Pattern | When you need it | Uses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Lists, tables and cards](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-lists-tables-and-cards) | Showing a collection: compare, read in order, or pick one | Table, MediaObject, InteractiveCard, Grid, InfiniteList |
| [Search, filtering and sorting](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-search-filtering-and-sorting) | Helping people find and narrow down items | TextField, Popover, CheckboxGroup, Tag, Table |
| [Tables and grids](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-tables-and-grids) | Rows to read, sort, select or page through | Table, Pagination, InfiniteList, EmptyState |
| [Dashboards and summaries](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-dashboards-and-summaries) | An overview screen, or a summary of one record | Alert, Stat, Card, Grid, charts |
| [Data visualization](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-data-visualization) | A figure, a trend, a chart or a dashboard | Stat, Sparkline, LineChart, AreaChart, BarChart, DonutChart, ScatterChart, Meter |

## Whole screens

The [Examples] are complete
screens built from these patterns: a dashboard, sign-in, a long registration
form, a sighting report, an instalment plan and a secretary work queue.

guides.title: Page layouts and app shells
guides.summary: Most screens are one of a few shapes: a signed-in app with navigation, a page of content to read, a landing page made of bands, or a workspace of panels. Pick the shape first, then fill it. The parent owns placement and space; components size themselves.
guides.text:
# Page layouts and app shells Most screens are one of a few shapes: a signed-in app with navigation, a page of content to read, a landing page made of bands, or a workspace of panels. Pick the shape first, then fill it. The parent owns placement and space; components size themselves. ## Choosing a shape | The screen is… | Compose | Example | | --- | --- | --- | | A signed-in app: several sections people move between | `StickyHeader`, then a row of [Sidebar](squonk-ui://components/sidebar) with [NavList](squonk-ui://components/nav-list) and a `
` | [Member dashboard] | | A task: a form, a sighting report, a payment | The app shell, with the task in a narrow column ([Container](squonk-ui://components/container) `size="tablet"`) | [Log a sighting] | | A page to read: help, a policy, a statement | One column capped at a readable width, titled with [Heading](squonk-ui://components/heading)s | Below | | A landing or marketing page | [Page](squonk-ui://components/page) with a [Header](squonk-ui://components/header), [Section](squonk-ui://components/section)s and a [Footer](squonk-ui://components/footer) | [Cards and landing sections](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-cards-and-landing-sections) | | A workspace: a list and its detail, an editor and a preview | [ResizablePanels](squonk-ui://components/resizable-panels) inside the app shell | [Resizable workspaces](#resizable-panels-and-workspaces) | | A sign-in or a single focused step outside the app | A narrow [Card](squonk-ui://components/card) in the middle of the page ([Centered](squonk-ui://components/centered)) | [Member sign-in] | ## The app shell A header across the top, side navigation, and the page's own header over its content. The page header holds a [Breadcrumb](squonk-ui://components/breadcrumb), the page's `h1`, and its main actions in a [Split](squonk-ui://components/split), so the title and the actions part on wide screens and stack on narrow ones. **Example:** Sidebar with a NavList marking the current page, then the page header: breadcrumb, a heading that matches the navigation item, and one primary action. ```tsx export function AppShellExample() { const [current, setCurrent] = React.useState("sightings"); return (
({ ...item, href: `#${item.id}` }))} />
Sightings The page's content. Its heading matches the current navigation item.
); } const SHELL_NAV = [ { id: "overview", label: "Overview" }, { id: "sightings", label: "Sightings", end: 1 due }, { id: "payments", label: "Payments" }, { id: "settings", label: "Settings" }, ]; /** A reading page: one column capped at a readable width, titled sections. */ ``` - **One `
` per screen.** `Page` renders it; if you build the shell yourself, render your own `
` beside the Sidebar and don't nest a Page inside. - **Name each navigation** with NavList's `label`, and mark the current page with `current`. - **The heading matches the item.** The page's `h1` says the same as the navigation item that led there. - **On phones**, hide the Sidebar and open the same NavList in a [Drawer](squonk-ui://components/drawer) `placement="start"` from a menu IconButton in the header. Close it with NavList's `onNavigate`. - **One scroll area.** The main column scrolls; the header and sidebar stay put. Avoid a second scroll inside the page unless a region really needs one ([ScrollBox](squonk-ui://components/scroll-box)). ## A page to read Long text is hard to read across a wide screen. Cap the column at about 65 characters (`Container size="tablet"` or a `maxWidth`), use headings for each topic, and keep related actions at the end of the section they belong to. **Example:** One readable column, a heading for each topic. ```tsx export function ReadingColumnExample() { return (
Paying by instalments Spread your dues over regular payments. Who can apply Anyone with dues they can't pay in full by the due date. Apply before it's overdue if you can. What it costs The late fee stops growing while you keep to the plan.
); } // ---- Search, filtering and sorting -------------------------------------------- /** A labelled search above the results, filters in a popover, active filters as removable tags, and a count. */ ``` ## Landing pages Build a landing page from Sections. Each Section is a band with its own `register` and `tone`: `hero` for the opening, `default` or `large` for the bands after it, alternating `tone="surface"` to separate them. A [SectionHeading](squonk-ui://components/section-heading) introduces each band, and a [Grid](squonk-ui://components/grid) of Cards holds features or plans. Use `BleedSection` only for content that must run edge to edge. ## Resizable panels and workspaces Use [ResizablePanels](squonk-ui://components/resizable-panels) when people need to see two or three things at once and choose how much room each gets: a list and the selected item, a document and its notes, an editor and a preview. | Situation | Use | | --- | --- | | Navigation that's always the same width | [Sidebar](squonk-ui://components/sidebar), not a resizable panel | | A list and its detail, side by side, on a wide screen | `ResizablePanels` with two panels | | A side panel people sometimes want out of the way | A `collapsible` panel with a `minSize` | | A detail view that only some tasks need | A [Drawer](squonk-ui://components/drawer) instead, so the list keeps the room | | Two pieces of content that sit side by side and never change | A [Grid](squonk-ui://components/grid) or `Split` | ```tsx ``` - **Give the group a size.** It fills its container, so put it in a region with a height (the main column of the app shell, a fixed-height card). - **Name every handle** with `label` ("Resize case list"). Handles are reachable by Tab and move with the arrow keys, so keyboard users can resize too. - **Set limits.** A `minSize` stops a panel being squeezed until its content breaks; use a length such as `"16rem"` when the content has a natural width. - **Remember the layout.** Save what `onLayout` gives you and pass it back as `defaultLayout`, so people find the workspace as they left it. - **Stack on phones.** Below the tablet breakpoint, show one panel at a time (the list, then the detail as its own view) rather than squeezing panels side by side. ## Responsive behaviour Layouts are mobile first: one column by default, more as space allows. Use the theme's breakpoints (see [Space and layout](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-space-and-layout)) and let components respond to the space they're given. | Part | On a phone | From tablet (768px) | From desktop (1024px) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Side navigation | In a Drawer, opened from the header | Sidebar | Sidebar | | Page header | Title, then actions below it (Split wraps) | Title and actions on one row | Same | | Card and figure grids | One column | Two or three (`Grid columns={{ mobile: 1, tablet: 3 }}`) | Same, or more on `wide` | | Forms | One column, full-width fields | One column; pair short related fields | Same: forms don't need more columns | | Tables | Scroll sideways inside their own area, or show fewer columns | Full table | Full table | | Resizable panels | One panel at a time | Side by side | Side by side | - **Prefer fluid layouts** (`Grid minColumnWidth`, `Cluster`, `Split wrap`) over switching at breakpoints. They respond to the container, so a card in a narrow sidebar also works. - **Keep the reading order.** What stacks first on a phone should be what comes first in the source; never reorder visually with CSS alone. - **Touch targets** stay at least as big as the library makes them. Don't shrink controls on phones; use the `compact` register only where a pointer is likely. - **Test at real widths** (320px, 768px, 1280px) and with long content, not only at the window sizes you design for. ## Accessibility - Use landmarks: one `
`, named `
`s, one `
`, and a `
`. Header, Sidebar (`
`), Page (`
`) and Footer render them for you. - Give each page one `h1`, and headings that follow in order inside it. - Add a skip link to the main content when the navigation before it is long. - A Drawer used as the phone menu traps focus while open and returns it to the menu button when it closes; don't build your own. ## Pitfalls - **Nesting Pages.** `Page` is the viewport's root; render one per screen. - **Layout CSS before primitives.** Reach for Grid, Split, Cluster, VStack and Container before writing your own flex rules. - **Fixed heights for content.** Let content set the height; only workspaces and scroll areas need a fixed size. - **Resizable panels for everything.** If people never need to change the split, a fixed layout is simpler and more predictable. ## Related - [App navigation](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-app-navigation) - [Density and registers](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-density-and-registers) - [Choosing components](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-choosing-components)

guides.title: Printing
guides.summary: Some pages are printed: statements, receipts, sighting reports, newsletters, a plan to sign. The library prints every page well without any work: ink on white, no shadows or motion, no buttons, tables in full and link addresses shown. For a page people print on purpose, decide what belongs on paper with Printable, NotPrintable and PrintOnly.
guides.text:
# Printing

Some pages are printed: statements, receipts, sighting reports, newsletters, a plan to sign.
The library prints every page well without any work: ink on white, no shadows
or motion, no buttons, tables in full and link addresses shown. For a page
people print on purpose, decide what belongs on paper with
[Printable, NotPrintable and PrintOnly](squonk-ui://components/printable).

## The rules

- **Mark the record, not the rest.** Wrap what someone prints the page for in
  `Printable`: the statement, the receipt, the schedule. Everything else is left
  off without listing it.
- **Leave the screen's machinery off.** Navigation, filters, actions and help
  that only work on screen go in `NotPrintable` when the whole page prints.
- **Say on paper what the screen said another way.** A reference number, the
  date and time printed, who it's for, or a line replacing a control ("Pay
  online at …") go in `PrintOnly`.
- **Keep what belongs together on one page** with `keepTogether`, and start a
  new section on a fresh page with `breakBefore`.
- **Never print secrets the screen masked**: a printed page leaves your app's
  control.

## Choosing a mark

| You want to | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Print only part of the page | `Printable` around that part |
| Print the page without something | `NotPrintable` around that thing |
| Add something only to the printout | `PrintOnly` |
| Start a section on a new page | `<Printable breakBefore>` |
| Stop a block splitting across pages | `<Printable keepTogether>` |
| Mark part of a sentence | Any of them with `inline` |

## The theme on paper

The theme decides how paper looks. Its `printBackgrounds` switch keeps the
theme's own colours and backgrounds (for a branded receipt, say); left off, a
page prints in ink on white, whatever the theme or mode. `printLinkUrls`
(on by default) prints each web or email link's address after its text. The
colours paper uses are purpose tokens under `roles.print`, which a theme can
re-point one by one. See [Theme](squonk-ui://guides/foundations-theme).

## What your app owns

The browser owns the page size, the margins it offers, and the header and
footer it prints (the title, the address and page numbers), which readers can
turn off. Test a real printout or its PDF, in more than one browser, for any
page people rely on printing.

guides.title: QR handoff
guides.summary: Use QrCode to move someone from a screen to their phone. Say where it goes, and always offer another way in.
guides.text:
# QR handoff

Use [QrCode](squonk-ui://components/qr-code) to move someone from a screen
to their phone. Say where it goes, and always offer another way in.

**Example:** The code's purpose is stated, and people who can't scan get a link.

```tsx
export function QrHandoffExample() {
  return (
    <Cluster gap="lg" align="center">
      <QrCode value="https://example.org/app?ref=demo" label="Scan to open the app on your phone" />
      <VStack gap="xs" style={{ maxWidth: 280 }}>
        <Text weight="bold">Continue on your phone</Text>
        <Text tone="secondary">Scan the code with your phone's camera. It opens the app at your sighting report.</Text>
        <Link href="#send-link">Can't scan? Send me a link instead</Link>
      </VStack>
    </Cluster>
  );
}

// ---- Choosing a selection control ---------------------------------------------

const CHAPTERS = ["Northland", "Auckland", "Waikato", "Bay of Plenty", "Gisborne", "Hawke's Bay", "Taranaki", "Manawatū-Whanganui", "Wellington", "Tasman", "Nelson", "Marlborough", "West Coast", "Canterbury", "Otago", "Southland"].map((region) => ({ value: region.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z]+/g, "-"), label: `${region} Chapter` }));

/** Each control for the kind of choice it fits. */
```

## The rules

- **Say what happens when they scan** before they reach for their phone.
- **Offer another route**: a link to send, or a short code to type. Scanning
  isn't possible for everyone.
- **Never make scanning the only way** to complete a form or read essential text.
- **Keep the contrast and the quiet border** around the code, and test the real
  encoded value at the real size on a phone; a screenshot doesn't prove it scans.

Your app owns the link: that it's valid, that it expires, that it carries no
secrets, and what happens after the scan. A scanned code doesn't mean the task
is done or the destination is safe.

guides.title: Search, filtering and sorting
guides.summary: People find things in three ways: they type what they know (search), they narrow a list by what it is (filter), or they put it in an order (sort). Most collections need one or two of these, rarely all three at once. Compose them from TextField, Popover or Drawer, CheckboxGroup, Tag and Table.
guides.text:
# Search, filtering and sorting People find things in three ways: they type what they know (search), they narrow a list by what it is (filter), or they put it in an order (sort). Most collections need one or two of these, rarely all three at once. Compose them from [TextField](squonk-ui://components/text-field), [Popover](squonk-ui://components/popover) or [Drawer](squonk-ui://components/drawer), [CheckboxGroup](squonk-ui://components/checkbox-group), [Tag](squonk-ui://components/tag) and [Table](squonk-ui://components/table). ## Which one | People… | Give them | In `@squonkstack/ui` | | --- | --- | --- | | Know the name or number of what they want | A search field above the results | `TextField type="search"` with a visible label | | Pick one value from a long list inside a form | A searchable select, not a page search | [Select](squonk-ui://components/select) `searchable` | | Want only items of a kind (status, interest, owner) | Filters | One to three: [Select](squonk-ui://components/select)s in a row. More: [CheckboxGroup](squonk-ui://components/checkbox-group)s in a [Popover](squonk-ui://components/popover), or a [Drawer](squonk-ui://components/drawer) on phones | | Switch between a few fixed sets ("Open", "Closed", "All") | Views | [Tabs](squonk-ui://components/tabs), each with its count | | Want the newest, the biggest, A to Z | Sorting | Table `sortable` columns; a "Sort by" [Select](squonk-ui://components/select) for lists and cards | **Example:** Search by name, filter by interest in a popover, and see what's applied as removable tags with a count. Sort by any column. Search for something that isn't there to see the empty state. ```tsx export function SearchAndFilterExample() { const [query, setQuery] = React.useState(""); const [interests, setInterests] = React.useState([]); const rows = MEMBERS.filter((c) => (interests.length === 0 || interests.includes(c.interest)) && c.name.toLowerCase().includes(query.trim().toLowerCase())); const filtering = Boolean(query || interests.length); const clear = () => { setQuery(""); setInterests([]); }; return (
setQuery(e.target.value)} />
Filters {interests.length ? {interests.length} : null}} footer={} > ({ value: t, label: t }))} value={interests} onChange={setInterests} /> {filtering ? ( {rows.length} of {MEMBERS.length} members {query ? setQuery("")} removeLabel="Clear the search">“{query}” : null} {interests.map((t) => setInterests((list) => list.filter((x) => x !== t))}>{t})} ) : null} } title="No members match" body="Try a different name or fewer filters." action={} />} /> ); } const MEMBERS = [ { id: "c1", name: "Aroha Ngata", interest: "Night watches", due: "28 Nov" }, { id: "c2", name: "Tui Anderson", interest: "Tear-pool mapping", due: "20 Nov" }, { id: "c3", name: "Rimu Whānau Keepers", interest: "Folklore archive", due: "7 Apr" }, { id: "c4", name: "Moana Reid", interest: "Night watches", due: "15 Jan" }, ]; // ---- Lists, tables and cards -------------------------------------------------- /** A list: one line per item, read top to bottom, each with one link. */ ``` ## Search - **Label it** ("Search members"), and say what it searches in the placeholder or help text ("Name, case number or reason"). A magnifier icon alone isn't a label. - **Put it above what it searches**, and keep the results in the same place. - **Search as people type** for lists already in the browser (Table `filter` does this). For server searches, wait until they pause or press Enter, and show the results' state in words. - **Keep the query** in the field and, for whole pages, in the URL, so Back and sharing work. ## Filters - **Show what's applied.** Each active filter is a removable [Tag](squonk-ui://components/tag) in a `TagGroup`, with "Clear all" beside them. A count on the Filters button ("Filters 2") says some are on even when the panel is closed. - **Say how many match**: "3 of 12 members". Table announces its new row count when its `filter` changes; announce your own count for other lists. - **Apply at once** in a popover or panel beside the results. Use an "Apply" button only when each change is slow (a server query that takes seconds), and then say that nothing changes until it's pressed. - **Filters combine predictably**: values within one filter widen the results (Night watches *or* Folklore archive); different filters narrow them (Night watches *and* overdue). - **Never hide all results without saying why.** The empty state names the filters and offers to clear them. ## Sorting - **Sort tables by their headers.** Mark sortable columns with `sortable`, give derived values a `sortValue`, and start with a sensible `defaultSort` (usually the newest or the most urgent first). - **One sort at a time** is enough for almost every screen. - **Lists and card grids** have no headers, so sort them with a "Sort by" Select above the list, labelled with the order it gives ("Newest first"). ## Accessibility - Search and filter controls sit **before** the results in the reading order. - Changing a filter doesn't move focus. Announce the new count politely (a `role="status"` element), as Table does. - Removing a Tag returns focus to a sensible place in the group; don't rebuild the group in a way that drops focus. - Sortable headers are buttons and announce the current direction; don't add your own sort icons to a header that isn't sortable. ## Pitfalls - **Filters with no visible state.** If people can't see what's applied, they think records are missing. - **"No results" for a failed search.** A server error is an error, not an empty result; say so and offer to try again. - **A searchable Select as a page search.** It chooses one value for a form; it doesn't filter a list on the page. - **Too many filters up front.** Show the two or three people use most; put the rest in the panel. The [Society secretary] example puts it together: a search, filters in a popover, active filters as tags, bulk actions on selected rows and an empty state that clears everything. ## Related - [Tables and grids](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-tables-and-grids) - [Lists, tables and cards](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-lists-tables-and-cards) - [Empty and error states](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-empty-and-error-states)

guides.title: Settings and preferences
guides.summary: A settings page is a set of small, separate decisions that people come back to rarely and want to get right. Group them by topic, make it obvious when each change takes effect, and keep the risky ones apart. Compose Headings, Switch, RadioGroup, Select, Fieldset and Button.
guides.text:
# Settings and preferences

A settings page is a set of small, separate decisions that people come back to
rarely and want to get right. Group them by topic, make it obvious when each
change takes effect, and keep the risky ones apart. Compose
[Heading](squonk-ui://components/heading)s,
[Switch](squonk-ui://components/switch),
[RadioGroup](squonk-ui://components/radio),
[Select](squonk-ui://components/select),
[Fieldset](squonk-ui://components/fieldset) and
[Button](squonk-ui://components/button).

**Example:** Notifications save as they're switched. Statements are a small form with its own Save button that names what it saves.

```tsx
export function SettingsExample() {
  const [reminders, setReminders] = React.useState(true);
  const [frequency, setFrequency] = React.useState("monthly");
  const [saved, setSaved] = React.useState<string>();
  return (
    <VStack gap="xl" style={{ maxWidth: "36rem" }}>
      <section aria-labelledby="settings-notifications">
        <VStack gap="md">
          <VStack gap="xxs">
            <Heading level={4} as="h3" id="settings-notifications">Notifications</Heading>
            <Text tone="secondary">These change as soon as you switch them.</Text>
          </VStack>
          <Switch label="Email reminders" helperText="Before each due date." checked={reminders} onChange={setReminders} />
          <Switch label="Text message alerts" helperText="For payments and credits." defaultChecked={false} />
        </VStack>
      </section>
      <section aria-labelledby="settings-statements">
        <form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); setSaved("Statement preferences saved."); }}>
          <VStack gap="md">
            <VStack gap="xxs">
              <Heading level={4} as="h3" id="settings-statements">Statements</Heading>
              <Text tone="secondary">Saved when you press the button.</Text>
            </VStack>
            <RadioGroup name="statement-frequency" legend="How often" value={frequency} onChange={setFrequency} options={[{ value: "monthly", label: "Monthly" }, { value: "quarterly", label: "Quarterly" }]} />
            <Fieldset legend="Send to">
              <TextField label="Email" type="email" defaultValue="aroha@example.org" />
            </Fieldset>
            <Cluster gap="sm" align="center">
              <Button variant="primary" type="submit">Save statement preferences</Button>
              <Text as="span" tone="secondary" role="status">{saved ?? ""}</Text>
            </Cluster>
          </VStack>
        </form>
      </section>
    </VStack>
  );
}

// ---- Onboarding and first run -------------------------------------------------

/** A set-up checklist: progress in words and a bar, done steps marked, the next step as the one primary action. */
```

## Saving: at once, or with a button

| The setting… | Use | Saves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Turns one thing on or off ("Email reminders") | [Switch](squonk-ui://components/switch) | At once. Say "Saved", or move it back and say why if it fails |
| Is one choice from a few, with no side effects ("Theme: light, dark, system") | [RadioGroup](squonk-ui://components/radio) or [Select](squonk-ui://components/select) | At once, the same way |
| Is several fields that only make sense together (an address, a bank account) | A small form in its own section | With a button that names it: "Save address" |
| Is text people type | [TextField](squonk-ui://components/text-field) in a section form | With the section's button, never on each keystroke |
| Is hard to undo (cancel the membership, stop all newsletters) | A Button `danger` in its own section, last | After a [ConfirmModal](squonk-ui://components/modal) that names the consequence |

Say at the top of each section which kind it is ("These change as soon as you
switch them", "Saved when you press the button"). Never mix the two inside one
group. See [Switches, checkboxes and saving](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-switches-checkboxes-and-saving).

## Laying out a settings page

- **Group by topic**, each group a section with a heading and a one-line
  description: Contact details, Notifications, Security, Danger zone.
- **Long pages get a side navigation.** With more than five or six groups, add a
  [NavList](squonk-ui://components/nav-list) of the sections, or
  split them into pages under a settings section of the app.
- **One column.** Settings read top to bottom; keep them in a column capped at a
  readable width.
- **Destructive settings go last**, in their own section, with the consequence
  in words.

## Labels and help

Label the setting, not its state: "Email reminders", not "Reminders are on".
Use `helperText` for what changes ("Before each due date. You'll still get
notices.") and for anything people might worry about. See
[Writing for the interface](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-writing-for-the-interface).

## Accessibility

- Each section is a `<section>` named by its heading (`aria-labelledby`), so
  screen-reader users can move between groups.
- A switch that saves at once announces the result near itself (`role="status"`),
  not in a toast only.
- Related fields share a [Fieldset](squonk-ui://components/fieldset) with a
  legend that states the question.
- Don't disable a Save button to show nothing has changed; let it say "No
  changes to save" if pressed.

## Pitfalls

- **One Save button for the whole page.** People change one thing, scroll, and
  leave without saving. Save per section, or at once.
- **Switches in a form that saves later.** People can't tell whether anything
  changed.
- **Settings in a modal.** A settings page people return to deserves its own
  URL; use a modal only for one quick change.
- **Hidden consequences.** If a setting affects other people (a household member's
  access), say so beside it.

The [Account settings]
example shows each kind: a contact form with an error summary, switches that
save at once (one fails and moves back), statements saved by a button, signed-in
devices with a menu, and a confirmation that can't be dismissed while it works.

## Related

- [Switches, checkboxes and saving](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-switches-checkboxes-and-saving)
- [Destructive actions](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-destructive-actions)
- [Forms](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-forms-overview)

guides.title: Switches, checkboxes and saving
guides.summary: A Switch turns something **on or off**. A Checkbox **selects** something. The difference is what the user expects to happen when they press it.

guides.title: Tables and grids
guides.summary: Table has two modes. Choose by what people do with the rows, not by how many there are.
guides.text:
# Tables and grids

[Table](squonk-ui://components/table) has two modes. Choose by what people do
with the rows, not by how many there are.

## Static table (the default)

For reading and comparing. Screen readers navigate it with their own table
commands, links and buttons in cells stay in the normal tab order, and sortable
headers are buttons. Give it a `caption`.

**Example:** A reading table with a sortable column and statuses as badges.

```tsx
export function ReadingTableExample() {
  return <Table caption="Logged sightings" columns={sightingColumns} rows={SIGHTING_ROWS} rowKey="id" />;
}

/** A selectable grid: one tab stop, rows chosen to act on. */
```

Give each column explicit cells: object and derived fields need a `render`, and a
`sortValue` if the column sorts. Use a stable `rowKey` when rows change, align
numbers the same way down a column, and put real buttons or links in cells for
actions.

## Interactive grid

Turn it on with `selectable`, or `interactive` when cells hold controls. The
table becomes a grid with **one** tab stop: focus starts on a row, `↑`/`↓` move
between rows, `←`/`→` move into and between cells, `Space` selects a row, and
`Enter` on a sortable header sorts it. Use it when:

- people select rows to act on them, or
- most rows contain controls, so tabbing through every one would be tedious.

A grid changes how screen readers present the content, so don't use it just to
make a read-only table feel interactive. Never set `role="grid"` yourself; the
grid mode implements the whole interaction.

**Example:** Tab into the grid, move with the arrows, press Space to select a row.

```tsx
export function SelectableGridExample() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = React.useState<string[]>([]);
  return (
    <VStack gap="sm">
      <Cluster gap="sm" align="center">
        <Text weight="bold">{selected.length} selected</Text>
        <Button variant="secondary" disabled={selected.length === 0}>Download</Button>
      </Cluster>
      <Table caption="Sightings to download" columns={sightingColumns} rows={SIGHTING_ROWS} rowKey="id" selectable selectedKeys={selected} onSelectionChange={setSelected} />
    </VStack>
  );
}

/** An empty table that says which empty it is. */
```

## Paging or loading more

**Our guidance** (the sources compare neither):

- **Pages** (`pageSize`, or [Pagination](squonk-ui://components/pagination)
  for other lists) suit records people return to and refer to ("page 3"),
  and keep the footer reachable. The table announces each row's position across
  pages.
- **Loading as people scroll** ([InfiniteList](squonk-ui://components/infinite-list))
  suits feeds people skim once, newest first. It follows the WAI-ARIA feed pattern
  so keyboard users can jump past it.
- **Virtualising** is for very large client-side lists; the library doesn't
  provide it yet.

Filtering (`filter`) announces the new row count; keep the filter field outside
the table and above it.

## Empty and loading

Say which empty it is: no records yet ("Log your first sighting"), no matches
("No sightings match 'hemlock' — clear the filter") or no access. Pass that as
`empty`, often an [EmptyState](squonk-ui://components/empty-state). While
loading, show [Skeleton](squonk-ui://components/skeleton) rows in the
table's shape and keep existing rows visible during a refresh. Don't move focus
when data arrives.

**Example:** The empty slot says which empty it is, and how to get out of it.

```tsx
export function EmptyTableExample() {
  return (
    <Table
      caption="Sightings"
      columns={sightingColumns}
      rows={[]}
      rowKey="id"
      empty={<EmptyState icon={<FilterIcon />} title="No sightings match these filters" action={<Button variant="secondary">Clear filters</Button>} />}
    />
  );
}

// ---- Identity and metadata ----------------------------------------------------

/** A person: image or initials, name, role and a status in words. */
```

Table sorts, filters and pages rows in the browser. Your app owns fetching, and
server-side sorting or paging by passing `rows` in the order to show. It isn't an
editable data grid.

## Related

- [Focus management](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-focus-management)
- [Empty and error states](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-empty-and-error-states)

---

Sources, paraphrased: [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: table](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/table/)
and [grid](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/grid/), © W3C, under the
[W3C Software and Document License](https://www.w3.org/copyright/software-license/);
[React Aria Table](https://react-aria.adobe.com/Table), [React Spectrum TableView](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/v3/TableView.html)
and [Skeleton](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/Skeleton), © Adobe;
[Chakra UI v3 Table](https://chakra-ui.com/docs/components/table) (MIT).

guides.title: Toasts, alerts and dialogs
guides.summary: A toast disappears, may appear far from where the user is looking, and is easy to miss with a screen magnifier. Only use it for news the user can safely miss or can find again elsewhere.
guides.text:
# Toasts, alerts and dialogs

| The message… | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Confirms something the user just did and needs no action ("Invite sent") | A toast — [`useToast`](squonk-ui://components/toast) |
| Describes the state of this page or form and should stay until it changes | An inline [Alert](squonk-ui://components/alert) |
| Needs an answer before the user can continue | A dialog — [ConfirmModal](squonk-ui://components/modal) |

**Example:** The deadline is about this page, so it's an Alert. “Remind me” confirms with a toast. “Pay now” needs a decision first, so it asks.

```tsx
export function MessagesExample() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider position="bottom-right">
      <MessagesInner />
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}

function MessagesInner() {
  const toast = useToast();
  const [confirming, setConfirming] = React.useState(false);
  return (
    <VStack gap="md">
      <Alert tone="warning" title="Your annual dues are due in 3 days">Pay by 28 November to avoid a late fee.</Alert>
      <Cluster gap="sm">
        <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => toast.success("Reminder set for 26 November.")}>Remind me</Button>
        <Button variant="primary" onClick={() => setConfirming(true)}>Pay now</Button>
      </Cluster>
      <ConfirmModal
        open={confirming}
        title="Pay your annual dues?"
        message="You'll pay $85.00 by 28 November. You can switch to an instalment plan later."
        confirmLabel="Pay dues"
        cancelLabel="Go back"
        onCancel={() => setConfirming(false)}
        onConfirm={() => { setConfirming(false); toast.success("Dues paid."); }}
      />
    </VStack>
  );
}

/** Loading: skeleton for known shape, spinner for a short wait, a bar for measurable work. */
```

## Toasts are for things that can be missed

A toast disappears, may appear far from where the user is looking, and is easy to
miss with a screen magnifier. Only use it for news the user can safely miss or
can find again elsewhere.

- **Duration:** at least five seconds (the `ToastProvider` default). Timers
  pause while the user hovers or focuses the notifications and while the page is
  hidden.
- **Actions:** never make a toast the only way to do something. If a toast
  offers an action ("Undo"), keep the toast until dismissed (`duration: 0`) and
  offer the same action somewhere on the page.
- **Errors:** an error the user must fix belongs on the page, as an Alert or a
  field error. A toast can echo it.
- **Focus:** toasts never take focus. `Alt+T` reaches them from the keyboard.

The WAI-ARIA guidance goes further and says alerts should not disappear on their
own at all; we allow timed toasts for low-stakes confirmations only, which is
why the rules above are strict.

## Inline alerts stay put

An `Alert` sits next to the content it describes and stays until the situation
changes. Errors and warnings are announced assertively; information and success
politely. Don't move focus to an alert as it appears — except an error summary
after a failed submit, which the user needs next.

## Dialogs interrupt

Use a dialog only when the user must decide before continuing: confirming an
irreversible action, or resolving a conflict. See
[Destructive actions](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-destructive-actions).

## While something is happening

Show a wait where it happens, not as a toast: a
[Skeleton](squonk-ui://components/skeleton) when you know the shape of
what's coming, a [Spinner](squonk-ui://components/spinner) for a short
wait, a [ProgressBar](squonk-ui://components/progress-bar) when you can
measure progress, and a Button's `pending` for an action in flight. A toast can
say when long work has finished. See
[Loading and progress](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-loading-and-progress).

The toast queue is bounded: if losing a notification would matter, handle
`onOverflow`, and keep anything people must act on in the page too. Check busy,
success, failure, retry and leaving the page mid-way.

## Related

- [Loading and progress](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-loading-and-progress)
- [Empty and error states](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-empty-and-error-states)
- [Writing for the interface](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-writing-for-the-interface)

guides.text:
# Writing for the interface

The words are part of the design. Components make a screen accessible; only the
words make it clear. Write plainly, say what will happen, and use the same word
for the same thing everywhere. This page covers the wording (microcopy) you pass
to components: labels, buttons, messages, empty states and headings.

**Do:** The error says how to fix it, and the button says what it does.

```tsx
export function SpecificWordsExample() {
  return (
    <VStack gap="sm">
      <TextField label="Membership number" defaultValue="SQ-104" error="Enter all 6 digits, such as SQ-104-772" />
      <Cluster gap="sm"><Button variant="primary">Save bank account</Button><Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button></Cluster>
    </VStack>
  );
}

/** Vague words: the button says nothing about what happens, the error doesn't help. */
```

**Don't:** “Invalid input” doesn't help, and “OK” doesn't say what will happen.

```tsx
export function VagueWordsExample() {
  return (
    <VStack gap="sm">
      <TextField label="Membership number" defaultValue="SQ-104" error="Invalid input" />
      <Cluster gap="sm"><Button variant="primary">OK</Button><Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button></Cluster>
    </VStack>
  );
}

// ---- Density and registers -----------------------------------------------------

/** The same controls in the compact and default registers: everything steps together. */
```

## The basics

- **Plain words, short sentences.** Write for someone busy and reading on a
  phone. Use the words your users use, not internal names.
- **Sentence case** for everything: headings, labels, buttons, menu items
  ("Add a bank account", not "Add A Bank Account").
- **Say "you"** for the reader. Use "we" for the organisation, sparingly.
- **Front-load.** Put the important words first, so scanning and typeahead work.
- **Numbers as numerals** ("3 sightings"), dates people can't misread ("28
  November 2026"), money with its currency where it's ambiguous.

## Labels, buttons and messages, by component

| Text | Write | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Button | A verb and its object: what will happen | "Save address", "Log sighting", "Delete draft" |
| Link | Where it goes, readable on its own | "See all activity", not "Click here" |
| Field `label` | The thing being asked for, a noun | "Email", "Membership number" |
| `helperText` | Format, limits or why you're asking | "Starts with SQ, such as SQ-104-772" |
| Field `error` | What's wrong and how to fix it | "Enter a date in the past" |
| Fieldset `legend` | The question | "Which interests do you have?" |
| Heading | What the section or page is about | "Payment options" |
| Toast | What just happened, in the past tense | "Invite sent to Aroha" |
| Alert | What's going on, then what to do | "Your annual dues are due in 3 days. Pay by 28 November." |
| ConfirmModal | The question with its consequence; the action as the button | "Delete this draft? You can't undo this." with "Delete draft" |
| EmptyState | What would be here, and the next step | "No sightings yet" with "Log a sighting" |
| Badge | A state in one or two words | "Overdue", "3 new" |
| Switch label | The setting, not its state | "Email reminders" |
| Tooltip | A name or a few words, never instructions people need | "Search sightings" |

## Errors

- **Say what happened and what to do**, in that order. Don't blame the user.
- **Be specific**: "Enter an amount less than $10,000", not "Invalid value".
- **Don't say "error"** or show codes unless people need to quote them to
  support; then give the code after the plain words.
- **A failed load is not empty.** "We couldn't load your sightings. Try again."

## Consistent words

Pick one word for each thing and action and keep it: "Delete" or "Remove", not
both for the same thing; "Sighting report", not "Entry" on one screen and "Sighting report" on the
next. A button and the page it opens use the same words ("Add a bank account"
opens "Add a bank account").

## Accessibility

- Names must make sense out of context: screen readers list links, buttons and
  headings on their own.
- An icon-only control still needs words: IconButton's `label`.
- Say status in words as well as colour: a badge reads "Overdue", not only red.
- Avoid directions that depend on sight: "Select Save", not "Click the green
  button on the right".

## Pitfalls

- **Placeholders as labels or help.** They disappear when people type.
- **"Are you sure?"** Ask the real question with its consequence.
- **Marketing tone in a work screen.** "Awesome! You're all set!" adds nothing
  to "Sighting logged."
- **Words that change with state** on a control. A Switch's label stays the
  same whether it's on or off.

## Related

- [Labels, help and validation](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-labels-help-and-validation)
- [Empty and error states](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-empty-and-error-states)
- [Destructive actions](squonk-ui://guides/patterns-destructive-actions)
